```text
apply prove it works. run the real import flow and show me the written records.
```

Say two parallel attempts are about to write to the same branch:

```text
separate before serializing shared state. give each attempt its own worktree, no locks.
```

Each phrase lands because the rule behind it is specific. The agent still has to say, in its reply, which decision the rule changed. A principle citation with no decision behind it means the agent named the rule without applying it.

## The 24, briefly

The core principles decide how much to build and when to rethink the design:

- [Laziness Protocol](../../skills/principle-laziness-protocol/SKILL.md) prefers deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.
- [Foundational Thinking](../../skills/principle-foundational-thinking/SKILL.md) chooses the core data structures before writing logic.
- [Redesign from First Principles](../../skills/principle-redesign-from-first-principles/SKILL.md) integrates a new requirement as if it had been there from day one.
- [Attack the Premise](../../skills/principle-attack-the-premise/SKILL.md) writes down the premise that two or more failed fixes shared and tests it directly before the next fix.
- [Subtract Before You Add](../../skills/principle-subtract-before-you-add/SKILL.md) removes dead weight before building on top of it.
- [Minimize Reader Load](../../skills/principle-minimize-reader-load/SKILL.md) collapses layers and hidden state a reader must hold in their head.
- [Outcome-Oriented Execution](../../skills/principle-outcome-oriented-execution/SKILL.md) converges rewrites on the target design instead of preserving throwaway compatibility states.
- [Experience First](../../skills/principle-experience-first/SKILL.md) chooses the user's result over implementation convenience.
- [Exhaust the Design Space](../../skills/principle-exhaust-the-design-space/SKILL.md) builds two or three competing prototypes when there's no precedent.
- [Build the Lever](../../skills/principle-build-the-lever/SKILL.md) builds the script that does or proves the work, so a reviewer can rerun it. When an agent keeps doing the same thing by hand, have it write the tool or skill it wishes it had. If a script can do a step the same way every time, use the script, and save agents for the judgment calls.

The architecture principles decide where state, validation, and compatibility live:

- [Model the Domain](../../skills/principle-model-the-domain/SKILL.md) encodes repeated rules in one structure, not scattered conditionals.
- [Boundary Discipline](../../skills/principle-boundary-discipline/SKILL.md) validates at the boundary and trusts internal types.
- [Type System Discipline](../../skills/principle-type-system-discipline/SKILL.md) makes illegal states unrepresentable.
- [Make Operations Idempotent](../../skills/principle-make-operations-idempotent/SKILL.md) converges retries on the same end state.
- [Migrate Callers Then Delete Legacy APIs](../../skills/principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis/SKILL.md) migrates and deletes in one wave.
- [Separate Before Serializing Shared State](../../skills/principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state/SKILL.md) removes the sharing before adding coordination.

The verification principles define what counts as proof:

- [Prove It Works](../../skills/principle-prove-it-works/SKILL.md) verifies the real artifact, not a proxy.
- [Fix Root Causes](../../skills/principle-fix-root-causes/SKILL.md) reproduces and traces to the cause before changing code.
- [Sequence Work into Verifiable Units](../../skills/principle-sequence-verifiable-units/SKILL.md) ends each small unit in a check before starting the next.
- [Test Behavior, Not Implementation](../../skills/principle-test-behavior-not-implementation/SKILL.md) asserts what the code's users can observe, so a test fails when that behavior breaks and survives a change to the internals.
- [Explain the Number](../../skills/principle-explain-the-number/SKILL.md) names what limits a measured number and rules out that it measured something else, before anyone trusts or reports it. 1	# Make it yours
2	
3	poteto-mode is one person's style. The playbooks, routing, and model roles underneath it work just as well with yours. This page covers generating a personal mode, capturing lessons from a session, fixing the repo so agents stop repeating mistakes, authoring a focused skill, and testing a skill change before you trust it.
4	
5	Start smaller than you think. You don't need many skills on day one, or even this whole plugin. Prompt plainly, watch where agents fail, and add a skill or a check when the same failure shows up twice.
6	
7	## Generate your own mode with `/automate-me`
8	
9	```text
10	/automate-me
11	```
12	
13	You don't describe your style, because [`/automate-me`](../../skills/automate-me/SKILL.md) reads it out of your history. It mines your recent transcripts in the active workspace for repeated preferences, in how you like replies, delegation, verification, code, prose, and process, then asks you which patterns are really you. It drafts `.cursor/skills/<your-name>-mode/SKILL.md` through Cursor's built-in `create-skill` flow, runs the draft through [`/unslop`](../../skills/unslop/SKILL.md), and opens a PR from a worktree so you review it like any other change.
14	
15	Run it again whenever your habits drift:
16	
17	```text
18	/automate-me update my mode skill with everything since its last edit
19	```
20	
21	Update mode mines only the history since the skill last changed. It keeps rules you haven't contradicted, revises the ones with new evidence, and adds sections only for new patterns.
22	
23	## Capture a session's lessons with `/reflect`
24	
25	Right after a task that taught you something, run:
26	
27	```text
28	/reflect that took way too long. capture what we learned so the next run doesn't repeat it.
29	```
30	
31	[`/reflect`](../../skills/reflect/SKILL.md) sends the transcript to three parallel reviewers, then a synthesizer sorts the proposals into `Accepted`, `Rejected`, and `Backlog` and waits for your approval before any skill changes. Approve a proposal only if it would change a future decision. One weird session is an anecdote, not a rule.
32	
33	## Fix the environment with `/correct`
34	
35	When you correct agents for the same mistake again and again, the fix belongs in the repo, not in your next prompt. Rank the options by how well they hold:
36	
37	1. Make the mistake impossible with architecture or a better data structure.
38	2. Block it with types, or with a lint or CI check whose error names the fix.
39	3. Catch it with a test.
40	4. Write it down as a doc or agent rule. Nothing fails when an agent skips a rule, so this comes last.
41	
42	Human review isn't on the list. A reviewer who must catch the same mistake on every PR is the problem this fixes. [`/correct`](../../skills/correct/SKILL.md) does the work:
43	
44	```text
45	/correct agents keep calling the database client directly instead of going through the repository layer
46	```
47	
48	It reads recent commits, reverts, review comments, and comments that explain workarounds, then groups the mistakes into classes. A class counts once it has happened twice. It fixes the most frequent classes one commit each, at the highest level that works, and proves each new check fails on a real past mistake. It also keeps a table in the agent instruction file that pairs each rule with what enforces it, so a rule that nothing enforces shows up as a repeat. The reply lists each class with its evidence, the level chosen, and why a higher level didn't work.
49	
50	Run it with no argument and it finds the classes from history on its own. `/reflect` and `/correct` split the work. `/reflect` improves skills from one session. `/correct` changes the repo so a mistake class can't come back. Pair it with `/architect` when the fix is a new boundary. [Run many projects in parallel](./07-overnight.md#run-many-projects-in-parallel) has a prompt that does both across a whole repo.
51	
52	## Author a focused skill
53	
54	When you already know the workflow you want to capture:
55	
56	```text
57	/poteto-mode write a skill for verifying database migrations in this repo
58	```
59	
60	Writing a skill matches the [Authoring or modifying a skill playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/authoring-a-skill.md), which routes through Cursor's built-in `create-skill`, validates the frontmatter and links, and ships the result through the Opening a PR playbook. Agent-facing prose has a higher bar than human prose, because an unhelpful sentence becomes an instruction some future agent follows. Let the playbook hold that bar rather than writing a `SKILL.md` freehand.
61	
62	Two special cases have their own generators. A skill that must drive your app and prove behavior is a verification skill, so use [`/create-verification-skill`](../../skills/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md) and [`/maintain-verification-skill`](../../skills/maintain-verification-skill/SKILL.md) instead. A skill that checks a property of your code with a model checker, a proof, or another verifier is a formal verification skill, so use [`/create-formal-verification-skill`](../../skills/create-formal-verification-skill/SKILL.md). [Verify and ship](./06-verify-and-ship.md#create-a-project-verification-skill) covers both kinds.
63	
64	## Write docs to a standard with `/technical-writing`
65	
66	Skills aren't the only prose you ship. For docs, RFCs, readmes, PR descriptions, and commit messages:
67	
68	```text
69	/technical-writing review the readme changes
70	```
71	
72	[`/technical-writing`](../../skills/technical-writing/SKILL.md) applies a layered standard. Its goal is prose that a tired engineer understands on the first read. It picks the document's mode first (tutorial, how-to, reference, or explanation), then works sentence by sentence: who does what, one thought per sentence, nothing readable two ways. Use it to review what you or an agent just wrote, or name it up front when you ask for a doc.
73	
74	## Test a skill change blind
75	
76	A skill edit affects every future session, so test it like the experiment it is. The same goes for adopting someone else's skill. Check that it makes the agent better on your work before you keep it.
77	
78	```text
79	/poteto-mode run the eval playbook on this skill change. same task for both variants, candidates stay blind.
80	```
81	
82	When a skill keeps missing and you know what it should do, change and test it in one task:
83	
84	```text
85	/poteto-mode update the review skill so it flags missing migrations, and eval the change.
86	```
87	
88	Asking for the eval up front keeps the edit honest. A fix written from one bad session tends to overfit that session, and over many edits the skill drifts. The eval catches the drift before it ships.
89	
90	The [Eval playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/eval.md) is built around one failure mode, the observer effect. An agent that knows it's being evaluated behaves differently. So candidate agents get an organic-looking task in sanitized directories, never the words "eval" or "candidate", and never each other's existence. One judge scores all outputs under neutral labels, and chain-following gets graded from which files each candidate actually read, not from what it claims.
91	
92	Read every output yourself before accepting the verdict. If you disagree with the judge, suspect the rubric before you suspect your judgment.
93	
94	## Build a bot UI with `/make-bot-ui`
95

# Make it yours

poteto-mode is one person's style. The playbooks, routing, and model roles underneath it work just as well with yours. This page covers generating a personal mode, capturing lessons from a session, fixing the repo so agents stop repeating mistakes, authoring a focused skill, and testing a skill change before you trust it.

Start smaller than you think. You don't need many skills on day one, or even this whole plugin. Prompt plainly, watch where agents fail, and add a skill or a check when the same failure shows up twice.

## Generate your own mode with `/automate-me`

```text
/automate-me
```

You don't describe your style, because [`/automate-me`](../../skills/automate-me/SKILL.md) reads it out of your history. It mines your recent transcripts in the active workspace for repeated preferences, in how you like replies, delegation, verification, code, prose, and process, then asks you which patterns are really you. It drafts `.cursor/skills/<your-name>-mode/SKILL.md` through Cursor's built-in `create-skill` flow, runs the draft through [`/unslop`](../../skills/unslop/SKILL.md), and opens a PR from a worktree so you review it like any other change.

Run it again whenever your habits drift:

```text
/automate-me update my mode skill with everything since its last edit
```

Update mode mines only the history since the skill last changed. It keeps rules you haven't contradicted, revises the ones with new evidence, and adds sections only for new patterns.

## Capture a session's lessons with `/reflect`

Right after a task that taught you something, run:

```text
/reflect that took way too long. capture what we learned so the next run doesn't repeat it.
```

[`/reflect`](../../skills/reflect/SKILL.md) sends the transcript to three parallel reviewers, then a synthesizer sorts the proposals into `Accepted`, `Rejected`, and `Backlog` and waits for your approval before any skill changes. Approve a proposal only if it would change a future decision. One weird session is an anecdote, not a rule.

## Fix the environment with `/correct`

When you correct agents for the same mistake again and again, the fix belongs in the repo, not in your next prompt. Rank the options by how well they hold:

1. Make the mistake impossible with architecture or a better data structure.
2. Block it with types, or with a lint or CI check whose error names the fix.
3. Catch it with a test.
4. Write it down as a doc or agent rule. Nothing fails when an agent skips a rule, so this comes last.

Human review isn't on the list. A reviewer who must catch the same mistake on every PR is the problem this fixes. [`/correct`](../../skills/correct/SKILL.md) does the work:

```text
/correct agents keep calling the database client directly instead of going through the repository layer
```

It reads recent commits, reverts, review comments, and comments that explain workarounds, then groups the mistakes into classes. A class counts once it has happened twice. It fixes the most frequent classes one commit each, at the highest level that works, and proves each new check fails on a real past mistake. It also keeps a table in the agent instruction file that pairs each rule with what enforces it, so a rule that nothing enforces shows up as a repeat. The reply lists each class with its evidence, the level chosen, and why a higher level didn't work.

Run it with no argument and it finds the classes from history on its own. `/reflect` and `/correct` split the work. `/reflect` improves skills from one session. `/correct` changes the repo so a mistake class can't come back. Pair it with `/architect` when the fix is a new boundary. [Run many projects in parallel](./07-overnight.md#run-many-projects-in-parallel) has a prompt that does both across a whole repo.

## Author a focused skill

When you already know the workflow you want to capture:

```text
/poteto-mode write a skill for verifying database migrations in this repo
```

Writing a skill matches the [Authoring or modifying a skill playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/authoring-a-skill.md), which routes through Cursor's built-in `create-skill`, validates the frontmatter and links, and ships the result through the Opening a PR playbook. Agent-facing prose has a higher bar than human prose, because an unhelpful sentence becomes an instruction some future agent follows. Let the playbook hold that bar rather than writing a `SKILL.md` freehand.

Two special cases have their own generators. A skill that must drive your app and prove behavior is a verification skill, so use [`/create-verification-skill`](../../skills/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md) and [`/maintain-verification-skill`](../../skills/maintain-verification-skill/SKILL.md) instead. A skill that checks a property of your code with a model checker, a proof, or another verifier is a formal verification skill, so use [`/create-formal-verification-skill`](../../skills/create-formal-verification-skill/SKILL.md). [Verify and ship](./06-verify-and-ship.md#create-a-project-verification-skill) covers both kinds.

## Write docs to a standard with `/technical-writing`

Skills aren't the only prose you ship. For docs, RFCs, readmes, PR descriptions, and commit messages:

```text
/technical-writing review the readme changes
```

[`/technical-writing`](../../skills/technical-writing/SKILL.md) applies a layered standard. Its goal is prose that a tired engineer understands on the first read. It picks the document's mode first (tutorial, how-to, reference, or explanation), then works sentence by sentence: who does what, one thought per sentence, nothing readable two ways. Use it to review what you or an agent just wrote, or name it up front when you ask for a doc.

## Test a skill change blind

A skill edit affects every future session, so test it like the experiment it is. The same goes for adopting someone else's skill. Check that it makes the agent better on your work before you keep it.

```text
/poteto-mode run the eval playbook on this skill change. same task for both variants, candidates stay blind.
```

When a skill keeps missing and you know what it should do, change and test it in one task:

```text
/poteto-mode update the review skill so it flags missing migrations, and eval the change.
```

Asking for the eval up front keeps the edit honest. A fix written from one bad session tends to overfit that session, and over many edits the skill drifts. The eval catches the drift before it ships.

The [Eval playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/eval.md) is built around one failure mode, the observer effect. An agent that knows it's being evaluated behaves differently. So candidate agents get an organic-looking task in sanitized directories, never the words "eval" or "candidate", and never each other's existence. One judge scores all outputs under neutral labels, and chain-following gets graded from which files each candidate actually read, not from what it claims.

Read every output yourself before accepting the verdict. If you disagree with the judge, suspect the rubric before you suspect your judgment.

## Build a bot UI with `/make-bot-ui`

One situational skill is for Grok Bot users. [`/make-bot-ui`](../../skills/make-bot-ui/SKILL.md) builds a small page whose buttons wake a bot over a webhook routine. For example, you could swipe through a review queue and have each swipe ask the bot to act on that item. A server on your machine holds the webhook's sender key, so the key never reaches the browser or the chat. The skill also covers exposing the page on Tailscale.

**Pitfall:** don't edit a skill mid-task because it's misbehaving. Fix it in its own PR and keep the task moving. A skill edit that ships tangled into feature work is invisible to review and impossible to evaluate.

Next: [Recipes and pitfalls](./10-recipes-and-pitfalls.md).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check or extend the `| Rule | Enforced by |` table in an agent instruction file.

  rule_table.py check AGENTS.md [--json]
  rule_table.py add AGENTS.md --rule TEXT --enforced-by TEXT

`check` flags every row whose enforcement is prose only (docs, AGENTS.md, "code
review", empty) and every row that names an enforcer file that does not exist.
Nothing fails when an agent skips prose, so a flagged rule that gets broken again
is a repeat: fix it higher up (architecture > types > lint that names the fix >
test). Exit 0 when every row is enforced by something that runs, 1 otherwise,
2 on usage errors.

`add` appends a row to the first rule table (creating a `## Rules` section if the
file has none) and prints how the new row classifies.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

NONE_VALUES = {"", "-", "--", "—", "–", "none", "n/a", "na", "nothing", "tbd", "todo", "?", "nobody"}

# Words that name something that runs and fails. Matched case-insensitively.
CHECK_WORDS = re.compile(
    r"\b(lint(?:er|s|ed|ing)?|eslint|ruff|flake8|pylint|mypy|pyright|tsc|clippy|"
    r"typecheck(?:er|ing)?|types?|typed|enum|newtype|tests?|unittest|pytest|jest|vitest|"
    r"go test|cargo test|ci|pre-commit|git hook|hook|schema|compiler|compile[sd]?|patlint|"
    r"import-linter|codemod|assert(?:ion)?s?|runtime check|architecture|module boundary|"
    r"private module|bounded_check|tla\+|model[- ]check(?:er)?|kani|verify-[\w-]+|check_[\w]+)\b",
    re.I,
)
# Words that only describe a human or an agent remembering to do something.
PROSE_WORDS = re.compile(
    r"\b(prose|docs?|documentation|agents\.md|claude\.md|readme|wiki|guidelines?|conventions?|"
    r"code review|reviews?|reviewers?|manual(?:ly)?|honou?r system|agent rules?|this file|"
    r"comments?|memory|instructions?|skills?|reminders?|by hand)\b",
    re.I,
)
CODE_SPAN = re.compile(r"`([^`]+)`")
PATHLIKE = re.compile(r"^(?:\./)?[\w.@-]+(?:/[\w.@-]+)*\.(?:py|sh|bash|js|mjs|cjs|ts|tsx|go|rs|rb|java|kt|json|toml|ya?ml|cfg|ini)$")
TOOL_PREFIX = re.compile(r"^(python3?|node|npx|npm|pnpm|yarn|make|go|cargo|bash|sh|\./|uv|tox|nox|pytest|ruff|mypy|tsc|eslint)\b")


def split_row(line: str) -> list[str]:
    """Split a markdown table row on unescaped pipes outside code spans."""
    cells, buf, in_code, i = [], [], False, 0
    s = line.strip()
    while i < len(s):
        ch = s[i]
        if ch == "\\" and i + 1 < len(s) and s[i + 1] == "|":
            buf.append("|")
            i += 2
            continue
        if ch == "`":
            in_code = not in_code
        if ch == "|" and not in_code:
            cells.append("".join(buf).strip())
            buf = []
        else:
            buf.append(ch)
        i += 1
    cells.append("".join(buf).strip())
    if cells and cells[0] == "" and s.startswith("|"):
        cells = cells[1:]
    if cells and cells[-1] == "" and s.endswith("|"):
        cells = cells[:-1]
    return cells


def is_separator(line: str) -> bool:
    cells = split_row(line)
    return bool(cells) and all(re.fullmatch(r":?-{3,}:?", c.replace(" ", "")) for c in cells)


def find_tables(lines: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
    """Return every table whose header has a Rule column and an Enforced-by column."""
    tables = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines) - 1:
        line = lines[i]
        if line.lstrip().startswith("|") and is_separator(lines[i + 1]):
            header = [c.lower() for c in split_row(line)]
            rule_idx = next((k for k, c in enumerate(header) if re.match(r"^rules?\b", c)), None)
            enf_idx = next((k for k, c in enumerate(header) if "enforc" in c), None)
            j = i + 2
            rows = []
            while j < len(lines) and lines[j].lstrip().startswith("|"):
                rows.append((j + 1, split_row(lines[j])))
                j += 1
            if rule_idx is not None and enf_idx is not None:
                tables.append({"header_line": i + 1, "last_line": j, "rule_idx": rule_idx,
                               "enf_idx": enf_idx, "ncols": len(header), "rows": rows})
            i = j
            continue
        i += 1
    return tables


def git_toplevel(path: Path) -> Path | None:
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(path), "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
                             capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
        return Path(out) if out else None
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
        return None


def referenced_paths(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Path-like tokens inside code spans, including script paths inside commands."""
    found = []
    for span in CODE_SPAN.findall(text):
        for tok in span.split():
            tok = tok.strip("'\"(),;")
            if PATHLIKE.match(tok) or ("/" in tok and PATHLIKE.match(tok.split("::")[0])):
                found.append(tok.split("::")[0])
    return found


def classify(enforced_by: str, bases: list[Path]) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Return (status, reason). status is enforced | prose | none | missing-enforcer."""
    text = enforced_by.strip()
    if text.strip("`*_ ").lower() in NONE_VALUES:
        return "none", "nothing enforces this rule"
    paths = referenced_paths(text)
    missing = [p for p in paths if not any((b / p).exists() for b in bases)]
    if missing:
        return "missing-enforcer", "enforcer not found: " + ", ".join(missing)
    spans = CODE_SPAN.findall(text)
    runnable_span = any(TOOL_PREFIX.match(s.strip()) or PATHLIKE.match(s.strip()) for s in spans)
    if paths or runnable_span or CHECK_WORDS.search(text):
        return "enforced", "names a check that runs" if not paths else "runs " + ", ".join(paths)
    if PROSE_WORDS.search(text):
        return "prose", "enforced only by prose or human attention"
    return "prose", "names no check that runs (lint, type, test, CI, script)"


def check(path: Path) -> dict:
    lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines()
    tables = find_tables(lines)
    bases = [path.parent.resolve()]
    top = git_toplevel(path.parent.resolve())
    if top and top not in bases:
        bases.append(top)
    rows = []
    for t in tables:
        for lineno, cells in t["rows"]:
            if len(cells) <= max(t["rule_idx"], t["enf_idx"]):
                cells = cells + [""] * (max(t["rule_idx"], t["enf_idx"]) + 1 - len(cells))
            rule = cells[t["rule_idx"]]
            enf = cells[t["enf_idx"]]
            if not rule.strip():
                continue
            status, reason = classify(enf, bases)
            rows.append({"line": lineno, "rule": rule, "enforced_by": enf, "status": status, "reason": reason})
    flagged = [r for r in rows if r["status"] != "enforced"]
    return {"file": str(path), "tables": len(tables), "rules": rows, "flagged": len(flagged),
            "ok": bool(tables) and not flagged}


def escape_cell(text: str) -> str:
    return text.replace("|", "\\|").replace("\n", " ").strip()


def add(path: Path, rule: str, enforced_by: str) -> dict:
    row = f"| {escape_cell(rule)} | {escape_cell(enforced_by)} |"
    if path.exists():
        lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    else:
        lines = [f"# {path.stem}", ""]
    tables = find_tables(lines)
    if tables:
        t = tables[0]
        cells = [""] * t["ncols"]
        cells[t["rule_idx"]] = escape_cell(rule)
        cells[t["enf_idx"]] = escape_cell(enforced_by)
        row = "| " + " | ".join(cells) + " |"
        lines.insert(t["last_line"], row)
    else:
        if lines and lines[-1].strip():
            lines.append("")
        lines += ["## Rules", "", "| Rule | Enforced by |", "|---|---|", row]
    path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    bases = [path.parent.resolve()]
    top = git_toplevel(path.parent.resolve())
    if top:
        bases.append(top)
    status, reason = classify(enforced_by, bases)
    return {"file": str(path), "row": row, "status": status, "reason": reason}


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="rule_table.py",
        description="Check or extend the `| Rule | Enforced by |` table in AGENTS.md (or CLAUDE.md). "
                    "`check` exits 1 when a rule is enforced only by prose or names an enforcer that does not exist.",
        epilog="examples:\n"
               "  rule_table.py check AGENTS.md\n"
               "  rule_table.py check AGENTS.md --json\n"
               "  rule_table.py add AGENTS.md --rule 'Write todos only through store.save()' \\\n"
               "      --enforced-by '`python3 scripts/patlint.py --rules lint-rules.json todo/`'\n\n"
               "Enforced: names a lint, type, test, CI job, hook, schema, or an existing script/test file in backticks.\n"
               "Flagged:  prose, docs, AGENTS.md, code review, empty, or a backticked path that does not exist.",
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
    )
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    c = sub.add_parser("check", help="flag rules enforced only by prose (exit 1 if any)")
    c.add_argument("file", type=Path, help="agent instruction file, e.g. AGENTS.md")
    c.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="machine-readable output")
    a = sub.add_parser("add", help="append a row to the rule table")
    a.add_argument("file", type=Path)
    a.add_argument("--rule", required=True, help="the rule, phrased as what to do")
    a.add_argument("--enforced-by", required=True, help="what fails when the rule is broken (command, test, lint id)")
    a.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    if args.cmd == "check":
        if not args.file.is_file():
            print(f"rule_table: {args.file} not found. Create it with `rule_table.py add {args.file} --rule ... --enforced-by ...`.",
                  file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        res = check(args.file)
        if args.json:
            print(json.dumps(res, indent=2))
        else:
            if not res["tables"]:
                print(f"{args.file}: no `| Rule | Enforced by |` table. Add one: every rule paired with the check that fails when it is broken.")
            else:
                print(f"{args.file}: {len(res['rules'])} rules, {res['flagged']} flagged")
                for r in res["rules"]:
                    tag = {"enforced": "OK", "prose": "PROSE", "none": "NONE", "missing-enforcer": "MISSING"}[r["status"]]
                    print(f"  {tag:<8} line {r['line']:<4} {r['rule'][:70]}")
                    if r["status"] != "enforced":
                        print(f"           enforced by: {r['enforced_by'] or '(empty)'} -> {r['reason']}")
                if res["flagged"]:
                    print("FAIL: move each flagged rule up the pyramid (architecture > types > lint that names the fix > test), "
                          "then name that check in the Enforced by column. Drop rules whose mistake can no longer happen.")
                else:
                    print("PASS: every rule names a check that runs.")
        return 0 if res["ok"] else 1

    res = add(args.file, args.rule, args.enforced_by)
    if args.json:
        print(json.dumps(res, indent=2))
    else:
        print(f"added to {res['file']}: {res['row']}")
        if res["status"] != "enforced":
            print(f"warning: {res['status']}: {res['reason']}. This rule will fail `rule_table.py check`.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Normalize review feedback into one list where every item names its source.

Inputs:
  --repo REPO           git history: fix commits, reverts, and the commits they revert
  --pr-comments JSON    PR review comments in `gh api` shape (body/path/line/user/html_url);
                        concatenated pages from `gh api --paginate` work too. Repeatable.
  --chat MD             chat or meeting notes in markdown; each bullet or paragraph is one item. Repeatable.

Output (--out, default stdout): {"version", "repo", "generated_at", "inputs", "counts", "items": [...]}
Each item: {id, source (commit|review|chat|code-comment), ref (sha, URL, or file:line), text, paths, line,
author, date, url, kind (commits: fix|revert|reverted), diff_added/diff_removed (commits)}.

Uses the item readers from the sibling `correct` skill (correct/scripts/mine_mistakes.py),
so /correct and /feedback-to-architecture read evidence the same way.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime as dt
import json
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path


def load_mine_mistakes():
    here = Path(__file__)
    for base in (here.resolve().parent, here.parent):
        cand = base.parent.parent / "correct" / "scripts"
        if (cand / "mine_mistakes.py").is_file():
            sys.path.insert(0, str(cand))
            import mine_mistakes  # noqa: PLC0415
            return mine_mistakes
    sys.exit("collect_feedback: needs the `correct` skill installed next to this one "
             "(skills/correct/scripts/mine_mistakes.py). Run install.sh from poteto-skills.")


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="collect_feedback.py",
        description="Normalize PR review comments, commit-history signals, and chat notes into one feedback.json "
                    "where every item has a source and a ref.",
        epilog="examples:\n"
               "  gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/pulls/comments --paginate > review-comments.json   # read-only\n"
               "  collect_feedback.py --repo . --pr-comments review-comments.json --chat chat-feedback.md --out feedback.json\n"
               "  collect_feedback.py --repo . --since 2026-07-01 --out feedback.json\n"
               "next: plan.py feedback.json --out-dir refactor/",
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
    )
    ap.add_argument("--repo", required=True, type=Path, help="repository (git history is read from here)")
    ap.add_argument("--pr-comments", action="append", type=Path, default=[], metavar="JSON",
                    help="PR review comments, gh api JSON shape (repeatable)")
    ap.add_argument("--chat", action="append", type=Path, default=[], metavar="MD",
                    help="chat/meeting notes in markdown (repeatable)")
    ap.add_argument("--since", help="only commits after this date (YYYY-MM-DD or git --since syntax)")
    ap.add_argument("--max-commits", type=int, default=2000, help="newest N commits to read (default 2000)")
    ap.add_argument("--no-git", action="store_true", help="skip commit history")
    ap.add_argument("--code-comments", action="store_true", help="also include HACK/WORKAROUND/FIXME/XXX comments")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, help="write feedback.json here (default: stdout)")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    mm = load_mine_mistakes()
    repo = args.repo.resolve()
    if not repo.is_dir():
        print(f"collect_feedback: {repo} is not a directory", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    items: list[dict] = []
    git_used = False
    if not args.no_git:
        if mm.is_git_repo(repo):
            items += mm.git_items(repo, args.since, args.max_commits)
            git_used = True
            if args.code_comments:
                items += mm.code_comment_items(repo)
        else:
            print(f"collect_feedback: {repo} is not a git repo; skipping commit history", file=sys.stderr)
    for f in args.pr_comments:
        if not f.is_file():
            print(f"collect_feedback: --pr-comments {f} not found", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        got = mm.load_feedback(f, source="review")
        for it in got:
            if it["source"] == "chat":  # a markdown file passed as review comments
                it["source"] = "review"
        items += got
    for f in args.chat:
        if not f.is_file():
            print(f"collect_feedback: --chat {f} not found", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        items += mm.markdown_items(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), f.name, "chat")

    seen, out_items, dropped = set(), [], 0
    for it in items:
        if not it.get("source") or not it.get("ref"):
            dropped += 1
            continue
        if it["id"] in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(it["id"])
        out_items.append(it)
    if dropped:
        print(f"collect_feedback: dropped {dropped} item(s) without a source ref", file=sys.stderr)

    doc = {
        "version": 1,
        "tool": "collect_feedback",
        "repo": str(repo),
        "generated_at": dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=0).isoformat(),
        "inputs": {"git": git_used, "since": args.since, "pr_comments": [str(p) for p in args.pr_comments],
                   "chat": [str(p) for p in args.chat]},
        "counts": dict(Counter(it["source"] for it in out_items)),
        "items": out_items,
    }
    text = json.dumps(doc, indent=2, default=str) + "\n"
    if args.out:
        args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        args.out.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        counts = ", ".join(f"{v} {k}" for k, v in sorted(doc["counts"].items())) or "no items"
        print(f"collect_feedback: wrote {args.out} ({counts})", file=sys.stderr)
    else:
        sys.stdout.write(text)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

    ap.add_argument("--max-commits", type=int, default=2000, help="newest N commits to read (default 2000)")
    ap.add_argument("--no-git", action="store_true", help="skip commit history")
    ap.add_argument("--code-comments", action="store_true", help="also include HACK/WORKAROUND/FIXME/XXX comments")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, help="write feedback.json here (default: stdout)")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    mm = load_mine_mistakes()
    repo = args.repo.resolve()
    if not repo.is_dir():
        print(f"collect_feedback: {repo} is not a directory", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    items: list[dict] = []
    git_used = False
    if not args.no_git:
        if mm.is_git_repo(repo):
            items += mm.git_items(repo, args.since, args.max_commits)
            git_used = True
            if args.code_comments:
                items += mm.code_comment_items(repo)
        else:
            print(f"collect_feedback: {repo} is not a git repo; skipping commit history", file=sys.stderr)
    for f in args.pr_comments:
        if not f.is_file():
            print(f"collect_feedback: --pr-comments {f} not found", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        got = mm.load_feedback(f, source="review")
        for it in got:
            if it["source"] == "chat":  # a markdown file passed as review comments
                it["source"] = "review"
        items += got
    for f in args.chat:
        if not f.is_file():
            print(f"collect_feedback: --chat {f} not found", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        items += mm.markdown_items(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), f.name, "chat")

    seen, out_items, dropped = set(), [], 0
    for it in items:
        if not it.get("source") or not it.get("ref"):
            dropped += 1
            continue
        if it["id"] in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(it["id"])
        out_items.append(it)
    if dropped:
        print(f"collect_feedback: dropped {dropped} item(s) without a source ref", file=sys.stderr)

    doc = {
        "version": 1,
        "tool": "collect_feedback",
        "repo": str(repo),
        "generated_at": dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=0).isoformat(),
        "inputs": {"git": git_used, "since": args.since, "pr_comments": [str(p) for p in args.pr_comments],
                   "chat": [str(p) for p in args.chat]},
        "counts": dict(Counter(it["source"] for it in out_items)),
        "items": out_items,
    }
    text = json.dumps(doc, indent=2, default=str) + "\n"
    if args.out:
        args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        args.out.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        counts = ", ".join(f"{v} {k}" for k, v in sorted(doc["counts"].items())) or "no items"
        print(f"collect_feedback: wrote {args.out} ({counts})", file=sys.stderr)
    else:
        sys.stdout.write(text)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Turn feedback.json into REFACTOR_PLAN.md and patlint rules.

  plan.py feedback.json --out-dir DIR [--min-count 2] [--threshold 0.3] [--no-prove]

Clusters feedback items into themes (the same clustering /correct uses), keeps
themes seen at least --min-count times, and for each theme writes: evidence,
the pyramid level chosen (architecture > types > lint > test > docs) and why
not higher, a draft target design, steps, and proof commands.

For themes where the evidence names a bad pattern and the fix (from review
wording like "don't X, use Y" and from fix-commit diffs: removed lines = bad,
added lines = good), it writes a patlint rule to DIR/lint-rules.json. Unless
--no-prove, it replays every rule against the repo's own history: a rule is
`proven` when it reports more hits at the mistake revision than at the fixed
revision (fix commit: sha^ vs sha; reverted commit: sha vs sha^).

Outputs: DIR/REFACTOR_PLAN.md, DIR/lint-rules.json, DIR/plan.json.
Needs the sibling `correct` skill (mine_mistakes.py, patlint.py).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime as dt
import json
import re
import shlex
import subprocess
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path


def correct_scripts() -> Path:
    here = Path(__file__)
    for base in (here.resolve().parent, here.parent):
        cand = base.parent.parent / "correct" / "scripts"
        if (cand / "mine_mistakes.py").is_file() and (cand / "patlint.py").is_file():
            return cand
    sys.exit("plan: needs the `correct` skill installed next to this one "
             "(skills/correct/scripts/{mine_mistakes,patlint}.py). Run install.sh from poteto-skills.")


CORRECT = correct_scripts()
sys.path.insert(0, str(CORRECT))
import mine_mistakes as mm  # noqa: E402
import patlint  # noqa: E402

TOKEN = r"`?([A-Za-z_][\w./-]*(?:\(\))?)`?"
CODE_TOKEN = re.compile(r"^(?:[A-Za-z_]\w*(?:\.[A-Za-z_]\w*)+(?:\(\))?|[A-Za-z_]\w*\(\)|[\w-]+\.(?:json|ya?ml|toml|csv|db|sqlite|txt|ini|cfg))$")
DATAFILE = re.compile(r"\.(json|ya?ml|toml|csv|db|sqlite|txt|ini|cfg)$", re.I)
SOURCE_EXT = re.compile(r"\.(py|js|jsx|ts|tsx|mjs|cjs|go|rs|rb|java|kt|swift|cs|php|c|cc|cpp|h)$")
GOOD_PATS = [
    re.compile(r"\b(?:use|call|via|through|prefer|switch to|route (?:it )?through|go(?:es)? through|must use|"
               r"should use|always use)\s+(?:the\s+|a\s+)?" + TOKEN, re.I),
    re.compile(TOKEN + r"\s+instead\b(?!\s+of)", re.I),
]
BAD_PATS = [
    re.compile(r"\b(?:don'?t|do not|never|avoid|stop|no more|shouldn'?t|should not)\s+(?:use\s+|call\s+|using\s+|"
               r"calling\s+)?(?:the\s+)?" + TOKEN, re.I),
    re.compile(TOKEN + r"\s+(?:file\s+)?(?:directly|by hand)\b", re.I),
]
INSTEAD_OF = re.compile(TOKEN + r"\s+instead of\s+(?:using\s+|calling\s+)?" + TOKEN, re.I)
USE_BEFORE = re.compile(r"\b(?:use|call|prefer|switch to)\s+(?:the\s+)?$", re.I)

ARCH_SIGNALS = re.compile(
    r"\b(directly|bypass\w*|instead of|go(?:es)? through|route[sd]? through|only (?:place|module|way|writer)|"
    r"single source|source of truth|owner\w*|duplicat\w*|copy[- ]?past\w*|two ways|old way|legacy|deprecated|"
    r"internal|private|hand[- ]?sync\w*|by hand)\b", re.I)
TYPE_SIGNALS = re.compile(
    r"\b(status|state|transition\w*|enum|none|null|nil|optional|invalid|illegal|typo|string literal|magic string|"
    r"stringly|types?|typed|schema|validat\w*|unrepresentable)\b", re.I)
TEST_SIGNALS = re.compile(
    r"\b(regression|crash\w*|broke|broken|returns?|edge case|off[- ]by[- ]one|500|exception|traceback|flaky|race|"
    r"wrong (?:result|output|value))\b", re.I)
TEST_GLOBS = ["**/tests/**", "**/test/**", "**/test_*.py", "**/*_test.py", "**/*_test.go", "**/*.test.*", "**/*.spec.*"]


def norm(tok: str) -> str:
    return tok.strip().rstrip(".,;:").removesuffix("()").lower()


def clean(tok: str) -> str:
    return tok.strip().rstrip(".,;:")


def vote_tokens(items: list[dict]) -> tuple[list[str], list[str], dict]:
    """Return (bad, good, detail) code tokens for a theme, by majority vote."""
    good, bad = Counter(), Counter()
    surface: dict[str, Counter] = {}

    def add(counter: Counter, tok: str, w: int) -> None:
        tok = clean(tok)
        if not CODE_TOKEN.match(tok):
            return
        key = norm(tok)
        counter[key] += w
        surface.setdefault(key, Counter())[tok] += 1

    texts = [it.get("text") or "" for it in items]
    for text in texts:
        for pat in GOOD_PATS:
            for m in pat.finditer(text):
                add(good, m.group(1), 1)
        for pat in BAD_PATS:
            for m in pat.finditer(text):
                add(bad, m.group(1), 1)
        for m in INSTEAD_OF.finditer(text):
            x, y = m.group(1), m.group(2)
            if USE_BEFORE.search(text[: m.start()]):
                add(good, x, 1)
                add(bad, y, 1)
            else:
                add(bad, x, 1)
                add(good, y, 1)
    mentioned = " ".join(texts).lower()
    diff_seen = Counter(norm(t) for it in items for t in set(it.get("diff_ids") or []))
    for it in items:
        if it.get("source") != "commit":
            continue
        added = {clean(t) for t in it.get("diff_added") or []}
        removed = {clean(t) for t in it.get("diff_removed") or []}
        only_added, only_removed = added - removed, removed - added
        kind = it.get("kind")
        bad_side, good_side = (only_added, only_removed) if kind == "reverted" else (only_removed, only_added)
        for t in bad_side:
            if norm(t) in mentioned or diff_seen[norm(t)] >= 2:
                add(bad, t, 2)
        for t in good_side:
            if norm(t) in mentioned or diff_seen[norm(t)] >= 2:
                add(good, t, 2)
    keys = set(good) | set(bad)
    margin = {k: bad[k] - good[k] for k in keys}
    bad_toks = sorted((k for k in keys if margin[k] > 0), key=lambda k: (-margin[k], k))
    good_toks = sorted((k for k in keys if margin[k] < 0), key=lambda k: (margin[k], k))

    def best(k: str) -> str:
        return surface[k].most_common(1)[0][0]

    detail = {best(k): {"bad": bad[k], "good": good[k]} for k in sorted(keys)}
    return [best(k) for k in bad_toks], [best(k) for k in good_toks], detail


def choose_level(items: list[dict], bad: list[str], good: list[str]) -> tuple[str, str, str]:
    """(level, why, why_not_higher)."""
    text = " ".join(it.get("text") or "" for it in items)
    arch = len(ARCH_SIGNALS.findall(text))
    typ = len(TYPE_SIGNALS.findall(text))
    test = len(TEST_SIGNALS.findall(text))
    if good and arch >= 2:
        return ("architecture",
                f"the evidence describes bypassing an owner ({arch} owner/bypass signals) and names the supported way `{good[0]}`",
                "already the highest level; keep the lint as a ratchet while call sites migrate")
    if typ >= 2:
        return ("types",
                f"the evidence is about values or states that should not be writable ({typ} state/type signals)",
                "no single owner or bypass is named, so moving code alone would not stop the bad state being constructed")
    if bad and good:
        return ("lint",
                f"a concrete bad pattern (`{bad[0]}`) and its fix (`{good[0]}`) are named, but no ownership or state change is implied",
                "no owner/bypass or state signal in the evidence; a lint whose message names the fix is the cheapest check that fails")
    if test or bad:
        return ("test",
                "the evidence describes behavior that broke, with no code pattern a regex can catch",
                "no owner, type, or lintable pattern is named; a behavior test through the public entry point is the highest check that fits")
    return ("docs",
            "no code token, owner, or state signal: this reads as a judgment call",
            "nothing in the evidence can be checked mechanically yet; write one AGENTS.md line with a failure example and re-run /correct when it repeats")


def slug(s: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", s.lower().removesuffix("()")).strip("-")[:40] or "rule"


def owner_module(good: str) -> str | None:
    core = good.removesuffix("()")
    if DATAFILE.search(core):
        return None
    if "." in core:
        return core.split(".")[0]
    return None


def derive_rule(n: int, title: str, items: list[dict], bad: list[str], good: list[str]):
    bad = [b for b in bad if b.removesuffix("()") not in {g.removesuffix("()") for g in good}][:3]
    if not bad:
        return None, "no bad code pattern named in the evidence"
    if not good:
        return None, "the evidence never names the fix; choose the owner API (/architect) before adding a lint"
    paths = [p for it in items for p in (it.get("paths") or [])]
    exts = Counter(m.group(1) for p in paths for m in [SOURCE_EXT.search(p)] if m)
    include = [f"**/*.{e}" for e, _ in exts.most_common(2)] or ["**/*"]
    exclude = list(TEST_GLOBS)
    owner = owner_module(good[0])
    owner_globs = [f"**/{owner}.{e}" for e, _ in exts.most_common(2)] if owner else []
    exclude = owner_globs + exclude
    parts = ["\\b" + re.escape(b.removesuffix("()")) + "\\b" for b in bad]
    regex = parts[0] if len(parts) == 1 else "(?:" + "|".join(parts) + ")"
    rid = f"no-{slug(bad[0])}" + (f"-outside-{slug(owner)}" if owner else "")
    bad_txt = ", ".join(f"`{b}`" for b in bad)
    owner_txt = f" ({owner_globs[0].removeprefix('**/')} owns this)" if owner_globs else ""
    message = f"Use `{good[0]}` instead of {bad_txt}{owner_txt}. Theme T{n}: {title}."
    rule = {"id": rid, "regex": regex, "include": include, "exclude": exclude, "message": message}
    return rule, None


def mistake_revs(it: dict) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
    sha, kind = it.get("ref"), it.get("kind")
    if it.get("source") != "commit" or not sha:
        return None
    if kind == "reverted":
        return sha, sha + "^"
    return sha + "^", sha  # fix and revert commits: the mistake is in the parent


def count_hits(patlint_py: Path, rules_file: Path, repo: Path, rule_id: str, rev: str | None, paths: list[str]):
    cmd = [sys.executable, str(patlint_py), "--rules", str(rules_file), "--root", str(repo)]
    if rev:
        cmd += ["--rev", rev]
    cmd += paths
    res = subprocess.run(cmd + ["--json"], capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=str(repo))
    shown = shlex.join(cmd)
    if res.returncode not in (0, 1):
        return None, shown, res.stderr.strip().splitlines()[-1:] or ["error"]
    data = json.loads(res.stdout)
    hits = [v for v in data["violations"] + data["expired"] + data["invalid_exceptions"] if v["rule"] == rule_id]
    return len(hits), shown, [f"{v['path']}:{v['line']}" for v in hits[:5]]


def prove(rule: dict, items: list[dict], rules_file: Path, repo: Path) -> dict:
    patlint_py = CORRECT / "patlint.py"
    inc = [patlint.glob_to_regex(g) for g in rule["include"]]
    proof = {"replays": [], "proven": False, "head_hits": None, "head_cmd": None}
    for it in items:
        revs = mistake_revs(it)
        if not revs:
            continue
        paths = [p for p in it.get("paths") or [] if any(g.match(p) for g in inc)]
        if not paths:
            continue
        bad_rev, good_rev = revs
        before, cmd, where = count_hits(patlint_py, rules_file, repo, rule["id"], bad_rev, paths)
        after, _, _ = count_hits(patlint_py, rules_file, repo, rule["id"], good_rev, paths)
        ok = before is not None and before > (after or 0)
        proof["replays"].append({"commit": it["ref"][:10], "kind": it.get("kind"), "mistake_rev": bad_rev,
                                 "fixed_rev": good_rev, "hits_at_mistake": before, "hits_at_fixed": after,
                                 "where": where, "cmd": cmd, "distinguishes": ok})
        proof["proven"] = proof["proven"] or ok
    n, cmd, where = count_hits(patlint_py, rules_file, repo, rule["id"], None, [str(repo)])
    proof["head_hits"], proof["head_cmd"], proof["head_where"] = n, cmd, where
    return proof


TARGETS = {
    "architecture": "Make `{owner}` the single owner: callers use `{good}`, nothing else touches what {bad} touched. "
                    "Hide or delete the second path (move the internals behind `{owner}`, delete copies an agent could imitate), "
                    "so a change that looks right from one file is right for the repo. Keep `{rule}` as a ratchet until no call site is left.",
    "types": "Model the values in this theme ({sig}) as a type the bad state cannot be written in: an enum or newtype plus "
             "one transition function owned by one module, validated once at the boundary. Callers stop passing raw strings.",
    "lint": "Add patlint rule `{rule}` whose message names `{good}`. Adopt a ratchet baseline if the pattern is already common.",
    "test": "Write one behavior test through the public entry point that reproduces the past failure ({refs}). "
            "It must fail on the mistake revision and pass on the fix.",
    "docs": "Judgment call: add one line to AGENTS.md with a concrete failure example from {refs}. Re-run /correct when it repeats.",
}
STEPS = {
    "architecture": ["Run /architect on the owner boundary: sketch the owner API ({good}) and the module layout, two candidates.",
                     "Route every call site through the owner; list them with the lint: `{lint_cmd}`.",
                     "Delete the old path and any helper an agent could copy.",
                     "Keep the lint with a baseline while migrating; drop the AGENTS.md rule once the lint makes the mistake unmergeable."],
    "types": ["Sketch the type (enum/newtype + transition table) with /architect.",
              "Convert the boundary (CLI/HTTP/storage parsing) to construct the type once; internal code takes the type.",
              "Make illegal transitions raise in one function; delete scattered string comparisons.",
              "Add a test that the illegal transition from the evidence is rejected."],
    "lint": ["Review the generated rule (regex, include/exclude) against the evidence.",
             "Run it on HEAD: `{lint_cmd}`; adopt a baseline if hits exist: add `--baseline .patlint-baseline.json --update-baseline`.",
             "Wire the same command into CI and the AGENTS.md rule table (`rule_table.py add`)."],
    "test": ["Write the failing test first against the mistake revision.",
             "Fix, then keep the test in the default test command."],
    "docs": ["Add the rule with an example to AGENTS.md (`rule_table.py add AGENTS.md --rule ... --enforced-by docs`).",
             "Expect `rule_table.py check` to flag it until something enforces it."],
}


def evidence_line(it: dict) -> str:
    return mm.describe_item(it)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="plan.py",
        description="Cluster feedback.json into themes and write REFACTOR_PLAN.md (evidence, pyramid level, target "
                    "design, steps, proof) plus lint-rules.json (patlint format) for lintable themes.",
        epilog="examples:\n"
               "  plan.py feedback.json --out-dir refactor/\n"
               "  plan.py feedback.json --out-dir refactor/ --no-prove --min-count 3\n"
               "then prove a rule by hand on a past mistake:\n"
               "  python3 <skills>/correct/scripts/patlint.py --rules refactor/lint-rules.json --rev SHA^ path/to/file.py",
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
    )
    ap.add_argument("feedback", type=Path, help="feedback.json from collect_feedback.py")
    ap.add_argument("--out-dir", required=True, type=Path, help="where to write REFACTOR_PLAN.md, lint-rules.json, plan.json")
    ap.add_argument("--min-count", type=int, default=2, help="minimum occurrences for a theme (default 2)")
    ap.add_argument("--threshold", type=float, default=0.3, help="cosine similarity to join a theme (default 0.3)")
    ap.add_argument("--repo", type=Path, help="repo for proofs (default: the repo recorded in feedback.json)")
    ap.add_argument("--no-prove", action="store_true", help="skip replaying rules against git history")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    if not args.feedback.is_file():
        print(f"plan: {args.feedback} not found; make it with collect_feedback.py", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    doc = json.loads(args.feedback.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    items = mm.review_items_from_json(json.dumps(doc), args.feedback.name)
    repo = (args.repo or Path(doc.get("repo") or ".")).resolve()
    can_prove = not args.no_prove and mm.is_git_repo(repo)
    out = args.out_dir
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    rules_file = out / "lint-rules.json"

    classes, unclassified = mm.cluster_items(items, args.threshold, args.min_count)
    themes, rules = [], []
    for n, c in enumerate(classes, 1):
        members = c["evidence"]
        title = " / ".join(c["signature"][:3]) or f"theme {n}"
        bad, good, votes = vote_tokens(members)
        level, why, why_not = choose_level(members, bad, good)
        rule, no_rule = derive_rule(n, title, members, bad, good)
        if rule:
            used = {r["id"] for r in rules}
            if rule["id"] in used:
                rule["id"] = f"{rule['id']}-t{n}"
            rules.append(rule)
        refs = ", ".join(m["ref"][:10] if m["source"] == "commit" else m["ref"] for m in members[:3])
        themes.append({"id": f"T{n}", "title": title, "count": c["count"], "sources": c["sources"],
                       "signature": c["signature"], "level": level, "why": why, "why_not_higher": why_not,
                       "bad": bad, "good": good, "votes": votes, "rule": rule, "no_rule_reason": no_rule,
                       "refs": refs, "evidence": members, "proof": None})

    rules_doc = {"rules": rules, "generated_by": "feedback-to-architecture/scripts/plan.py",
                 "source": str(args.feedback)}
    rules_file.write_text(json.dumps(rules_doc, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    if rules:
        try:
            patlint.load_rules(rules_file)
        except patlint.RulesError as e:
            print(f"plan: generated rules failed patlint validation:\n{e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        if can_prove:
            for t in themes:
                if t["rule"]:
                    t["proof"] = prove(t["rule"], t["evidence"], rules_file, repo)

    patlint_cmd = f"python3 {CORRECT / 'patlint.py'} --rules {rules_file} --root {repo} {repo}"
    lines = [
        "# Refactor plan: make repeated feedback impossible",
        "",
        f"Generated {dt.date.today().isoformat()} by `plan.py` from `{args.feedback}` "
        f"({len(items)} items: " + ", ".join(f"{v} {k}" for k, v in sorted(Counter(i['source'] for i in items).items())) + ")."
        f" Repo: `{repo}`.",
        "",
        "Each theme is a cluster of feedback seen at least "
        f"{args.min_count} times. Its level is the highest that can work: architecture > types > lint whose message "
        "names the fix > test > docs. Target designs are drafts; refine them with /architect before implementing.",
        "",
        "## Summary",
        "",
        "| Theme | Items | Level | Lint rule | Proof on history |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for t in themes:
        proof = "-"
        if t["proof"]:
            reps = t["proof"]["replays"]
            proof = (("proven on " + ", ".join(r["mistake_rev"] for r in reps if r["distinguishes"]))
                     if t["proof"]["proven"] else ("not proven" if reps else "no commit to replay"))
        rule_cell = f"`{t['rule']['id']}`" if t["rule"] else "none"
        lines.append(f"| {t['id']} {t['title']} | {t['count']} | {t['level']} | {rule_cell} | {proof} |")
    if not themes:
        lines.append(f"| - | - | - | - | no theme reached {args.min_count} occurrences |")
    for t in themes:
        r = t["rule"]
        fill = {"owner": (owner_module(t["good"][0]) if t["good"] else None) or (t["good"][0] if t["good"] else "the owner module"),
                "good": t["good"][0] if t["good"] else "the supported API",
                "bad": ", ".join(f"`{b}`" for b in t["bad"][:3]) or "the bypass",
                "rule": r["id"] if r else "a lint", "sig": ", ".join(t["signature"][:5]), "refs": t["refs"],
                "lint_cmd": patlint_cmd}
        lines += ["", f"## {t['id']}: {t['title']}", "",
                  f"Occurrences: {t['count']} ({', '.join(f'{k}×{v}' for k, v in sorted(t['sources'].items()))}). "
                  f"Signature: {', '.join(t['signature'][:6])}.", "", "### Evidence", ""]
        lines += [f"- {evidence_line(m)}" for m in t["evidence"]]
        lines += ["", "### Level", "",
                  f"**{t['level']}**: {t['why']}.", f"Why not higher: {t['why_not_higher']}."]
        if t["bad"] or t["good"]:
            lines.append(f"Named in evidence: bad {', '.join(f'`{b}`' for b in t['bad'][:3]) or '-'}; "
                         f"fix {', '.join(f'`{g}`' for g in t['good'][:3]) or '-'}.")
        lines += ["", "### Target design (draft)", "", TARGETS[t["level"]].format(**fill), "", "### Steps", ""]
        lines += [f"{i}. {s.format(**fill)}" for i, s in enumerate(STEPS[t["level"]], 1)]
        lines += ["", "### Proof", ""]
        if r:
            lines.append(f"Rule `{r['id']}` in `{rules_file}`: regex `{r['regex']}`, include {r['include']}, "
                         f"message: {r['message']}")
            p = t["proof"]
            if p:
                for rp in p["replays"]:
                    mark = "fires on the mistake and not on the fix" if rp["distinguishes"] else "does NOT distinguish mistake from fix"
                    lines.append(f"- {rp['kind']} {rp['commit']}: {rp['hits_at_mistake']} hit(s) at `{rp['mistake_rev']}`, "
                                 f"{rp['hits_at_fixed']} at `{rp['fixed_rev']}`: {mark}. Rerun: `{rp['cmd']}`")
                if not p["replays"]:
                    lines.append("- No commit in this theme touches a file the rule includes; prove it on a scratch "
                                 "copy of the mistake from the review comment.")
                lines.append(f"- HEAD: {p['head_hits']} hit(s) now"
                             + (f" ({', '.join(p['head_where'])})" if p.get("head_where") else "")
                             + f". Rerun: `{p['head_cmd']}`. After the refactor this must be 0, "
                               "or held by a ratchet baseline.")
            else:
                lines.append(f"- Not replayed (--no-prove or no git repo). Replay with patlint `--rev SHA^` on a fix commit's files.")
        else:
            lines.append(f"No lint rule: {t['no_rule_reason']}.")
            if t["level"] in ("types", "test"):
                lines.append("Prove the change with a test that fails on the mistake revision and passes after it.")
        lines.append("Record the enforcement: `rule_table.py add AGENTS.md --rule \"...\" --enforced-by \"...\"` "
                     "(from the correct skill).")
    if unclassified:
        lines += ["", "## Seen once (not a theme yet)", ""]
        lines += [f"- {evidence_line(m)}" for m in unclassified[:30]]
        if len(unclassified) > 30:
            lines.append(f"- … {len(unclassified) - 30} more in plan.json")
    (out / "REFACTOR_PLAN.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    plan_doc = {"version": 1, "feedback": str(args.feedback), "repo": str(repo), "themes": themes,
                "unclassified": unclassified, "rules_file": str(rules_file), "proved": can_prove}
    (out / "plan.json").write_text(json.dumps(plan_doc, indent=2, default=str) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    summary = {"out_dir": str(out), "themes": len(themes), "rules": [r["id"] for r in rules],
               "proven": [t["rule"]["id"] for t in themes if t["rule"] and t["proof"] and t["proof"]["proven"]],
               "levels": {t["id"]: t["level"] for t in themes},
               "files": [str(out / "REFACTOR_PLAN.md"), str(rules_file), str(out / "plan.json")]}
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
