---
name: curator
description: "Keep this skill collection current: diff upstream pstack against the snapshot, research the latest practice on coding-agent reliability (pstack, the inverted pyramid, verification skills, feature maps, formal verification, agent-friendly architecture), write sourced proposals daily, and weekly apply the best ones on a local branch that is committed only after scripts/verify.sh passes. Use for /curator, \"update the skills from upstream\", or as the collection's scheduled routine."
---

# Curator

The skills here are prose, layer 3 of the pyramid. The curator keeps them current without letting them drift into unsourced advice. Every proposal names a fetched source, the pyramid level it lands on, and a concrete change. Every applied change passes `scripts/verify.sh` before it is committed, on a local branch that is never pushed.

`$SKILL_DIR` is the directory holding this file. Paths like `proposals/` are relative to the poteto-skills checkout.

## Cadence

- **Daily: propose.** `$SKILL_DIR/scripts/curate.sh --propose` runs `upstream_diff.sh`, then a headless `claude -p --model opus --effort max` with [`references/curator-prompt.md`](references/curator-prompt.md). That writes `proposals/YYYY-MM-DD.md`, and `check_proposals.py --fetch` must pass (it re-requests every source URL).
- **Weekly: apply.** `$SKILL_DIR/scripts/curate.sh --apply` creates branch `curator/YYYY-MM-DD` in a separate git worktree. There, Claude implements at most three proposals, a CHANGELOG line is appended, and `scripts/verify.sh --run-examples` runs. The commit happens only if verify passes. A human reviews and merges.

```cron
17 6 * * *  /path/to/poteto-skills/skills/curator/scripts/curate.sh --propose
47 6 * * 1  /path/to/poteto-skills/skills/curator/scripts/curate.sh --apply
```

For a scheduled cloud agent instead of cron, use `references/curator-prompt.md` as the routine prompt. It proposes only.

## By hand

```bash
$SKILL_DIR/scripts/upstream_diff.sh                     # changed, new, and removed upstream pstack files and skills
$SKILL_DIR/scripts/curate.sh --propose --offline        # no LLM: proposals from the upstream diff alone
python3 $SKILL_DIR/scripts/check_proposals.py proposals/2026-10-19.md --fetch --skills-dir skills
$SKILL_DIR/scripts/curate.sh --apply --offline          # deterministic apply: sync changed upstream files into research/upstream/
```

Tests and dry runs should set `POTETO_CACHE` to a scratch dir and `POTETO_UPSTREAM_URL` to a local git repo, which keeps them off the network and out of `~/.cache`.

## Sources to watch

- @poteto on X: https://x.com/poteto (S1, S2 in `research/NOTES.md`)
- pstack in cursor/plugins: https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack, including its README, `skills/`, `docs/guide/`, and commit history (S3 to S19)
- Write-ups about pstack, such as https://barnabyrobson.org/on-pstack/ (S20). Fetch the original posts they cite before relying on them.
- Verification tools: TLA+ https://lamport.azurewebsites.net/tla/tla.html, Kani https://model-checking.github.io/kani/, Hypothesis https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io/
- Papers on coding-agent evaluation, verification, and repo guardrails (cite the abstract page you fetched), and the Claude Code and Cursor skill docs, since frontmatter fields and install paths change.

## Acceptance bar

1. Every proposal has a real URL that was fetched. Search snippets don't count, and `check_proposals.py --fetch` re-requests each URL.
2. Every proposal has a pyramid level. A change that makes a skill's output more deterministic (a script, lint, test, or type) beats more prose.
3. Every proposal names a concrete change to a named skill (or `new:<name>`, or `collection`).
4. An applied change passes `scripts/verify.sh`, adds a CHANGELOG line, and keeps MAPPING.md and each SKILL.md Sources footer in sync.
5. Upstream text is MIT (© 2026 Lauren Tan). Adapt it with credit; don't paste it wholesale.

Reject unsourced claims, prose that restates an existing rule, and anything that would add network access to a skill script other than the curator's.

## Safety

`curate.sh` never pushes and never touches your working tree: apply mode works in a git worktree under `$POTETO_CACHE/worktrees`. A failed verify deletes the branch and keeps the patch in `logs/curator/DATE.failed.patch`. Everything is logged to `logs/curator/DATE.log`.

## Sources

- research/NOTES.md §6 (curator rule: proposals with source URLs; every applied change goes through verify.sh and the CHANGELOG)
- S3 pstack README: https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/README.md
- S18 principle-build-the-lever: https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/principle-build-the-lever/SKILL.md
- S20 Barnaby Robson, "On pstack" (scheduled daily routines), secondary: https://barnabyrobson.org/on-pstack/

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the poteto-skills collection for Claude Code and/or Cursor.
# Only ever creates, updates, or removes <root>/<skill> entries for this collection's own skills.
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
usage: install.sh [--copy] [--target claude|cursor|both] [--project DIR] [--uninstall] [--force] [--dry-run]

Installs every skills/<name> of this checkout into:
  ~/.claude/skills/<name> and ~/.cursor/skills/<name>        (default)
  DIR/.claude/skills/<name> and DIR/.cursor/skills/<name>    (--project DIR)

  --copy        copy the files instead of symlinking (default: symlink, so `git pull` updates them)
  --target T    claude, cursor, or both (default: both)
  --project DIR install into a project instead of $HOME
  --uninstall   remove only entries this script installed (our symlinks, or copies with its marker file)
  --force       replace an existing entry with the same name that this script did not install
  --dry-run     print what would happen; change nothing

Other entries in the skills dirs (for example ~/.claude/skills/synced) are never touched.
Skills that share helpers (feedback-to-architecture uses correct; maintain-verification-skill uses
create-verification-skill) are always installed together.
exit: 0 done, 1 an entry was skipped because of a conflict, 2 usage error
EOF
}

mode=link target=both project="" uninstall=0 force=0 dry=0
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --copy) mode=copy; shift ;;
    --target) target="${2:-}"; shift 2 || { usage >&2; exit 2; } ;;
    --project) project="${2:-}"; shift 2 || { usage >&2; exit 2; } ;;
    --uninstall) uninstall=1; shift ;;
    --force) force=1; shift ;;
    --dry-run) dry=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "install.sh: unknown option $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
case "$target" in claude|cursor|both) ;; *) echo "install.sh: --target must be claude, cursor, or both" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac

src_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P)/skills"
[[ -d "$src_root" ]] || { echo "install.sh: $src_root not found" >&2; exit 2; }
if [[ -n "$project" ]]; then
  [[ -d "$project" ]] || { echo "install.sh: --project $project is not a directory" >&2; exit 2; }
  base="$(cd "$project" && pwd -P)"
else
  base="${HOME:?HOME is not set}"
fi
roots=()
[[ "$target" == claude || "$target" == both ]] && roots+=("$base/.claude/skills")
[[ "$target" == cursor || "$target" == both ]] && roots+=("$base/.cursor/skills")

marker=".poteto-skills-install"
skills=()
for d in "$src_root"/*/; do
  [[ -f "$d/SKILL.md" ]] && skills+=("$(basename "$d")")
done
[[ ${#skills[@]} -gt 0 ]] || { echo "install.sh: no skills found in $src_root" >&2; exit 2; }

run() {
  if [[ "$dry" == 1 ]]; then echo "[dry-run] $*"; else "$@"; fi
}

is_ours() {  # an entry we installed: a symlink into src_root, or a copy carrying our marker
  local dest="$1"
  if [[ -L "$dest" ]]; then
    local t
    t="$(readlink "$dest")"
    [[ "$t" == "$src_root/"* ]]
  else
    [[ -f "$dest/$marker" ]]
  fi
}

conflicts=0 changed=0
for root in "${roots[@]}"; do
  for name in "${skills[@]}"; do
    src="$src_root/$name"
    dest="$root/$name"
    if [[ "$uninstall" == 1 ]]; then
      if [[ -e "$dest" || -L "$dest" ]]; then
        if is_ours "$dest"; then
          run rm -rf "$dest"; echo "removed $dest"; changed=$((changed + 1))
        else
          echo "skip $dest: not installed by poteto-skills (left alone)"
        fi
      fi
      continue
    fi
    if [[ -L "$dest" && "$mode" == link && "$(readlink "$dest")" == "$src" ]]; then
      echo "ok   $dest -> $src"
      continue
    fi
    if [[ -e "$dest" || -L "$dest" ]]; then
      if is_ours "$dest" || [[ "$force" == 1 ]]; then
        run rm -rf "$dest"
      else
        echo "skip $dest: exists and was not installed by poteto-skills (use --force to replace it)"
        conflicts=$((conflicts + 1))
        continue
      fi
    fi
    [[ -d "$root" ]] || run mkdir -p "$root"
    if [[ "$mode" == link ]]; then
      run ln -s "$src" "$dest"
      echo "link $dest -> $src"
    else
      run cp -R "$src" "$dest"
      if [[ "$dry" == 1 ]]; then
        echo "[dry-run] write $dest/$marker"
      else
        printf 'installed-by: poteto-skills install.sh\nsource: %s\ndate: %s\n' "$src" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" > "$dest/$marker"
        find "$dest" -name '__pycache__' -type d -prune -exec rm -rf {} +
      fi
      echo "copy $dest <- $src"
    fi
    changed=$((changed + 1))
  done
done

action=$([[ "$uninstall" == 1 ]] && echo "uninstall" || echo "install")
echo "install.sh: $action done: ${#skills[@]} skill(s), ${#roots[@]} target dir(s), $changed change(s), $conflicts conflict(s)$([[ "$dry" == 1 ]] && echo ' (dry run, nothing changed)')"
[[ "$conflicts" == 0 ]]

  --uninstall   remove only entries this script installed (our symlinks, or copies with its marker file)
  --force       replace an existing entry with the same name that this script did not install
  --dry-run     print what would happen; change nothing

Other entries in the skills dirs (for example ~/.claude/skills/synced) are never touched.
Skills that share helpers (feedback-to-architecture uses correct; maintain-verification-skill uses
create-verification-skill) are always installed together.
exit: 0 done, 1 an entry was skipped because of a conflict, 2 usage error
EOF
}

mode=link target=both project="" uninstall=0 force=0 dry=0
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --copy) mode=copy; shift ;;
    --target) target="${2:-}"; shift 2 || { usage >&2; exit 2; } ;;
    --project) project="${2:-}"; shift 2 || { usage >&2; exit 2; } ;;
    --uninstall) uninstall=1; shift ;;
    --force) force=1; shift ;;
    --dry-run) dry=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "install.sh: unknown option $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
case "$target" in claude|cursor|both) ;; *) echo "install.sh: --target must be claude, cursor, or both" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac

src_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P)/skills"
[[ -d "$src_root" ]] || { echo "install.sh: $src_root not found" >&2; exit 2; }
if [[ -n "$project" ]]; then
  [[ -d "$project" ]] || { echo "install.sh: --project $project is not a directory" >&2; exit 2; }
  base="$(cd "$project" && pwd -P)"
else
  base="${HOME:?HOME is not set}"
fi
roots=()
[[ "$target" == claude || "$target" == both ]] && roots+=("$base/.claude/skills")
[[ "$target" == cursor || "$target" == both ]] && roots+=("$base/.cursor/skills")

marker=".poteto-skills-install"
skills=()
for d in "$src_root"/*/; do
  if [[ -f "$d/SKILL.md" ]]; then skills+=("$(basename "$d")"); fi
done
[[ ${#skills[@]} -gt 0 ]] || { echo "install.sh: no skills found in $src_root" >&2; exit 2; }

run() {
  if [[ "$dry" == 1 ]]; then echo "[dry-run] $*"; else "$@"; fi
}

is_ours() {  # an entry we installed: a symlink into src_root, or a copy carrying our marker
  local dest="$1"
  if [[ -L "$dest" ]]; then
    local t
    t="$(readlink "$dest")"
    [[ "$t" == "$src_root/"* ]]
  else
    [[ -f "$dest/$marker" ]]
  fi
}

conflicts=0 changed=0
for root in "${roots[@]}"; do
  for name in "${skills[@]}"; do
    src="$src_root/$name"
    dest="$root/$name"
    if [[ "$uninstall" == 1 ]]; then
      if [[ -e "$dest" || -L "$dest" ]]; then
        if is_ours "$dest"; then
          run rm -rf "$dest"; echo "removed $dest"; changed=$((changed + 1))
        else
          echo "skip $dest: not installed by poteto-skills (left alone)"
        fi
      fi
      continue
    fi
    if [[ -L "$dest" && "$mode" == link && "$(readlink "$dest")" == "$src" ]]; then
      echo "ok   $dest -> $src"
      continue
    fi
    if [[ -e "$dest" || -L "$dest" ]]; then
      if is_ours "$dest" || [[ "$force" == 1 ]]; then
        run rm -rf "$dest"
      else
        echo "skip $dest: exists and was not installed by poteto-skills (use --force to replace it)"

        continue
      fi
    fi

    fi

  done
done

action=$([[ "$uninstall" == 1 ]] && echo "uninstall" || echo "install")
echo "install.sh: $action done: ${#skills[@]} skill(s), ${#roots[@]} target dir(s), $changed change(s), $conflicts conflict(s)$([[ "$dry" == 1 ]] && echo ' (dry run, nothing changed)')"
[[ "$conflicts" == 0 ]]

# Skill to source mapping

Every skill traces back to source IDs in [research/NOTES.md](research/NOTES.md). Upstream pstack is MIT-licensed, © 2026 Lauren Tan. Verbatim snapshots of the files these skills adapt are in [research/upstream/](research/upstream/) (cursor/plugins @ `6b78e9f`, pstack 0.15.27), with the license at [research/upstream/PSTACK_LICENSE](research/upstream/PSTACK_LICENSE).

Pyramid layers (S1): 1 codebase improvements (architecture, types, invariants) > 2 static analysis (lint, tests, CI, verification) > 3 prose (rules, docs, skills) > 4 human review. Skills are layer 3. The last column says which higher layer each skill's output lands on.

| Skill | What it does | Upstream sources | Pyramid layer it pushes toward |
|---|---|---|---|
| `create-verification-skill` | Scans the repo (`scan_repo.py`), scaffolds `verify-<app>` with a feature map and a `control.sh` harness (`scaffold.py`), proves it once end to end, and gates it (`check_verify_skill.py`). | S4 [create-verification-skill](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md), S13 [guide 06](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/docs/guide/06-verify-and-ship.md), S17 [prove-it-works](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/principle-prove-it-works/SKILL.md), S18 [build-the-lever](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/principle-build-the-lever/SKILL.md), S1 [post](https://x.com/poteto/status/2111133080526495985) | 2: a committed, rerunnable verification harness with evidence, instead of ad hoc clicking |
| `maintain-verification-skill` | Deterministic drift check between the feature map and the source (`drift_check.py`: index, H2 contract, missing and dead routes and commands), then a required live pass and triage. | S5 [maintain-verification-skill](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/maintain-verification-skill/SKILL.md), S13 [guide 06](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/docs/guide/06-verify-and-ship.md), S20 [On pstack](https://barnabyrobson.org/on-pstack/) (secondary) | 2: map drift becomes an exit code; the live pass keeps the harness true |
| `correct` | Mines reverts, fix commits, and feedback into mistake classes (`mine_mistakes.py`), fixes each at the highest level, ships a rule-file lint with ratchet and expiring exceptions (`patlint.py`), and audits the rule table (`rule_table.py`). | S7 [correct](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/correct/SKILL.md), S15 [guide 09](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/docs/guide/09-make-it-yours.md), S16 [encode-lessons-in-structure](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/principle-encode-lessons-in-structure/SKILL.md), S1 [post](https://x.com/poteto/status/2111133080526495985) | 1 and 2: architecture and types first, then a lint whose message names the fix, proven on a real past mistake |
| `feedback-to-architecture` | Normalizes PR comments, commit signals, and chat notes (`collect_feedback.py`), clusters them into themes, and writes `REFACTOR_PLAN.md` plus patlint rules replayed against history (`plan.py`). | S1 [post](https://x.com/poteto/status/2111133080526495985) (project prompt), S7 [correct](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/correct/SKILL.md), S8 [architect](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/architect/SKILL.md) | 1: an agent-friendly re-architecture backed by data, with lint rules (2) as the backstop |
| `architect` | Ground, then sketch at least two structurally distinct candidates, screen them against red flags, decide, implement against the sketch, and scrap on a pattern. `sketch_check.py` gates the sketch. | S8 [architect](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/architect/SKILL.md), S14 [guide 08](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/docs/guide/08-principles.md), S1 [post](https://x.com/poteto/status/2111133080526495985) | 1: types, signatures, and module boundaries decided before code |
| `sharpen` | Restates the goal in your own words, the expert approach, over- and under-specification, and one outside check. `brief.py` writes and checks the brief. Covers in-your-own-words. | S9 [sharpen](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/sharpen/SKILL.md), S10 [in-your-own-words](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/in-your-own-words/SKILL.md), S1 [post](https://x.com/poteto/status/2111133080526495985) | 2: a runnable outside check fixed before the work, instead of a human judging it afterwards |
| `formal-verification` | Picks the costliest, least-tested promise, chooses the tool (TLA+, Kani, generated inputs), shows the check failing on broken variants, keeps findings as findings, and leaves a project skill. Ships `bounded_check.py` and `tla_available.sh`. | S6 [create-formal-verification-skill](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/create-formal-verification-skill/SKILL.md), S2 [launch post](https://x.com/poteto/status/2111926622278521253), S13 [guide 06](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/docs/guide/06-verify-and-ship.md) | 2: model checking and bounded verification with able-to-fail mutants |
| `curator` | Diffs upstream pstack (`upstream_diff.sh`), writes sourced proposals daily, and weekly applies them on a local branch that is committed only if `scripts/verify.sh` passes (`curate.sh`, `check_proposals.py`). | NOTES §6, S3 [pstack README](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/README.md), S18 [build-the-lever](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/principle-build-the-lever/SKILL.md), S20 [On pstack](https://barnabyrobson.org/on-pstack/) (secondary) | keeps layer 3 sourced; every change is gated by layer 2 (`verify.sh`) |

## Helper scripts

| Skill | Script | Output |
|---|---|---|
| create-verification-skill | `scan_repo.py REPO [--json]` | inventory: languages, build/test commands, launch candidates, routes, CLI subcommands, skill dirs, features |
| create-verification-skill | `scaffold.py REPO --app NAME [--skills-dir DIR]` | `verify-NAME/` with SKILL.md, `features/`, `scripts/control.sh`; unknowns as `TODO(verify)` |
| create-verification-skill | `check_verify_skill.py SKILL_DIR` | contract gate, exit 1 on any failure |
| maintain-verification-skill | `drift_check.py SKILL_DIR --repo REPO [--json]` | index, contract, missing and dead routes and commands; exit 1 on drift |
| correct | `mine_mistakes.py REPO [--since DATE] [--feedback FILE...] [--json]` | mistake classes (count >= 2) with commit shas and comment ids |
| correct | `patlint.py --rules RULES.json [--baseline FILE] [--update-baseline] PATHS...` | lint with ratchet and expiring inline exceptions; `--rev` replays history |
| correct | `rule_table.py check AGENTS.md` | flags rules enforced only by prose |
| feedback-to-architecture | `collect_feedback.py --repo REPO [--pr-comments JSON] [--chat MD] [--out FILE]` | `feedback.json`, every item with a source ref |
| feedback-to-architecture | `plan.py feedback.json --out-dir DIR` | `REFACTOR_PLAN.md`, `lint-rules.json`, `plan.json` |
| architect | `sketch_check.py SKETCH.md` | candidates, distinctness, red-flags screen, synthesis decision |
| sharpen | `brief.py "task"` / `brief.py --check BRIEF.md` | the brief, with candidate raw sources from the repo |
| formal-verification | `bounded_check.py MODEL.py [--mutants]` | BFS model check, shortest counterexample, mutant kill table |
| formal-verification | `tla_available.sh [--json]` | whether java and tla2tools.jar are present |
| curator | `upstream_diff.sh [--json]`, `curate.sh [--propose\|--apply] [--offline]`, `check_proposals.py FILE` | upstream report, proposals, local curator branch |

## Upstream material not adopted as skills

| Source | Why not, for now |
|---|---|
| S11 `recall` | Needs harness-specific transcript paths. `feedback-to-architecture` takes recurring corrections as a markdown input instead. |
| S12 `poteto-mode`, S14 principles | A personal router and a principle index. The principles that change outputs (build the lever, prove it works, encode lessons in structure) are folded into the skills above. |
| S19 Claude Code adapter | Install paths are handled by `install.sh`. |

# poteto-skills

Agent skills for Claude Code and Cursor that push their own output up the inverted pyramid. Each skill is prose, but what it leaves behind is a script, a lint rule, a test, a model check, or a type, so the next agent gets a check that fails instead of an instruction it can skip.

Built on [pstack](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack) by Lauren Tan ([@poteto](https://x.com/poteto)), MIT licensed. The skills here adapt pstack's ideas in new words and add deterministic helper scripts. See [Credits](#credits).

## The inverted pyramid

From Lauren Tan's [post](https://x.com/poteto/status/2111133080526495985) (S1 in [research/NOTES.md](research/NOTES.md)). Put the most effort into the top layer and the least into the bottom:

1. **Codebase improvements**: architecture, types, invariants, clear boundaries. Agents copy what exists and take the shortest path, so make the easy thing the right thing.
2. **Static analysis**: lint rules, tests, CI, verification (for example TLA+). Cheap, deterministic, run on every change.
3. **Prose**: comments, rules, AGENTS.md, skills. Use it minimally; nothing fails when it is ignored.
4. **Human review**: the hardest layer to scale. Spend it on designing an environment where agents do the right thing by default.

## Skills

| Skill | Use it for | Leaves behind |
|---|---|---|
| [`/create-verification-skill`](skills/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md) | an app agents can't yet launch, drive, and prove | `verify-<app>/` with a feature map and a `control.sh` harness (launch, doctor, drive, evidence, cleanup, prove) |
| [`/maintain-verification-skill`](skills/maintain-verification-skill/SKILL.md) | keeping that map honest, daily | a drift report (exit 1), a live pass, at most one PR |
| [`/correct`](skills/correct/SKILL.md) | mistakes agents repeat | mistake classes from history, `patlint` rules proven on past mistakes, an enforced rule table |
| [`/feedback-to-architecture`](skills/feedback-to-architecture/SKILL.md) | review feedback that keeps coming back | `REFACTOR_PLAN.md` plus lint rules replayed against git history |
| [`/architect`](skills/architect/SKILL.md) | non-trivial design | a checked `SKETCH.md`: two or more distinct candidates, a red-flag screen, a synthesis decision |
| [`/sharpen`](skills/sharpen/SKILL.md) | framing a task before starting (includes in-your-own-words) | a brief with one runnable outside check |
| [`/formal-verification`](skills/formal-verification/SKILL.md) | races, retries, state machines, parsers | a model with a one-command check and mutants that prove it can fail |
| [`/curator`](skills/curator/SKILL.md) | keeping this collection current | dated, sourced proposals and verified local `curator/` branches |

[MAPPING.md](MAPPING.md) maps each skill to its upstream sources and lists every helper script.

## Install

```bash
git clone <this repo> poteto-skills && cd poteto-skills
./install.sh --dry-run            # see what it would do
./install.sh                      # symlink every skill into ~/.claude/skills and ~/.cursor/skills
./install.sh --copy --target claude
./install.sh --project ~/code/app # into ~/code/app/.claude/skills and ~/code/app/.cursor/skills
./install.sh --uninstall          # removes only what install.sh created
```

`install.sh` only creates, updates, or removes entries named after this collection's skills, and it leaves anything it didn't install alone (for example `~/.claude/skills/synced`). Install all skills together: `feedback-to-architecture` reuses `correct`'s scripts, and `maintain-verification-skill` reuses `create-verification-skill`'s.

Requirements: Python 3.11+ (developed on 3.13) using the stdlib only, bash, and git. `gh` is optional, for reading PR comments. The curator also uses `curl` and, for its online steps, the `claude` CLI. TLA+ needs Java and `tla2tools.jar`; without them, `formal-verification` falls back to its stdlib `bounded_check.py`.

## Quick start

```bash
S=~/.claude/skills
python3 $S/correct/scripts/mine_mistakes.py . --since "90 days ago"
python3 $S/create-verification-skill/scripts/scan_repo.py .
python3 $S/create-verification-skill/scripts/scaffold.py . --app myapp
python3 $S/formal-verification/scripts/bounded_check.py $S/formal-verification/references/example_model.py --mutants
```

Then invoke a skill by name in your agent, for example `/correct agents keep writing the data file directly`.

## Layout

```text
skills/<name>/SKILL.md        frontmatter (name, description) + agent-facing body + Sources footer
skills/<name>/scripts/        executable helpers, stdlib Python or bash, all with --help
skills/<name>/references/     templates and worked examples
install.sh                    symlink or copy into Claude Code / Cursor skill dirs
research/                     NOTES.md (sources S1-S23) and verbatim upstream snapshots
examples/todo-app/            example repo the helpers are exercised against
scripts/verify.sh             the collection's self-check; scripts/run-examples.sh runs every helper for real
```

## Credits

The ideas, structure, and much of the vocabulary come from [pstack](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack) by Lauren Tan, © 2026, MIT license ([copy](research/upstream/PSTACK_LICENSE)). Snapshots of the upstream files these skills adapt are kept verbatim in [research/upstream/](research/upstream/) under that license. Each SKILL.md ends with a Sources footer that links the upstream files it draws on. The helper scripts are new to this collection.

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file. The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

## [0.1.0] - 2026-10-19

### Added

- `create-verification-skill`: `scan_repo.py` (Python AST, Node, Go, and Make heuristics for routes, CLI subcommands, ports, build/test commands), `scaffold.py` (writes `verify-<app>` with SKILL.md, a feature map using the four H2s, and a `control.sh` harness: launch, doctor, drive, evidence, cleanup, status, prove), and `check_verify_skill.py` (contract gate).
- `maintain-verification-skill`: `drift_check.py`, covering index hygiene, the H2 contract, and routes and commands missing from or dead in the map.
- `correct`: `mine_mistakes.py` (mistake classes from reverts, fix commits and their diffs, review comments, chat notes, and workaround comments), `patlint.py` (rule-file lint with a ratchet baseline, expiring inline exceptions, and `--rev` to replay history), and `rule_table.py` (flags rules enforced only by prose).
- `feedback-to-architecture`: `collect_feedback.py` (normalized `feedback.json`) and `plan.py` (`REFACTOR_PLAN.md`, `lint-rules.json`, and `plan.json`, with each rule replayed against git history).
- `architect`: `sketch_check.py`, plus a sketch template and a design red-flags list.
- `sharpen`: `brief.py` (writes and checks the brief; covers in-your-own-words).
- `formal-verification`: `bounded_check.py` (stdlib explicit-state model checker with counterexample traces, deadlock detection, `--mutants`, and `--expect-violation`), `tla_available.sh`, and an example lost-update model.
- `curator`: `upstream_diff.sh`, `curate.sh` (daily propose, weekly apply on a local `curator/<date>` worktree branch, committed only after `scripts/verify.sh` passes, never pushed), `check_proposals.py`, and `references/curator-prompt.md`.
- `install.sh` with symlink and `--copy` modes, `--target claude|cursor|both`, `--project`, `--uninstall`, `--force`, and `--dry-run`.
- README.md, MAPPING.md, and this changelog.

[Unreleased]: #unreleased

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file. The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

## [0.1.0] - 2026-10-19

### Added

- `create-verification-skill`: `scan_repo.py` (Python AST, Node, Go, and Make heuristics for routes, CLI subcommands, ports, build/test commands), `scaffold.py` (writes `verify-<app>` with SKILL.md, a feature map using the four H2s, and a `control.sh` harness: launch, doctor, drive, evidence, cleanup, status, prove), and `check_verify_skill.py` (contract gate).
- `maintain-verification-skill`: `drift_check.py`, covering index hygiene, the H2 contract, and routes and commands missing from or dead in the map.
- `correct`: `mine_mistakes.py` (mistake classes from reverts, fix commits and their diffs, review comments, chat notes, and workaround comments), `patlint.py` (rule-file lint with a ratchet baseline, expiring inline exceptions, and `--rev` to replay history), and `rule_table.py` (flags rules enforced only by prose).
- `feedback-to-architecture`: `collect_feedback.py` (normalized `feedback.json`) and `plan.py` (`REFACTOR_PLAN.md`, `lint-rules.json`, and `plan.json`, with each rule replayed against git history).
- `architect`: `sketch_check.py`, plus a sketch template and a design red-flags list.
- `sharpen`: `brief.py` (writes and checks the brief; covers in-your-own-words).
- `formal-verification`: `bounded_check.py` (stdlib explicit-state model checker with counterexample traces, deadlock detection, `--mutants`, and `--expect-violation`), `tla_available.sh`, and an example lost-update model.
- `curator`: `upstream_diff.sh`, `curate.sh` (daily propose, weekly apply on a local `curator/<date>` worktree branch, committed only after `scripts/verify.sh` passes, never pushed), `check_proposals.py`, and `references/curator-prompt.md`.
- `install.sh` with symlink and `--copy` modes, `--target claude|cursor|both`, `--project`, `--uninstall`, `--force`, and `--dry-run`.
- README.md, MAPPING.md, and this changelog.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Turn feedback.json into REFACTOR_PLAN.md and patlint rules.

  plan.py feedback.json --out-dir DIR [--min-count 2] [--threshold 0.3] [--no-prove]

Clusters feedback items into themes (the same clustering /correct uses), keeps
themes seen at least --min-count times, and for each theme writes: evidence,
the pyramid level chosen (architecture > types > lint > test > docs) and why
not higher, a draft target design, steps, and proof commands.

For themes where the evidence names a bad pattern and the fix (from review
wording like "don't X, use Y" and from fix-commit diffs: removed lines = bad,
added lines = good), it writes a patlint rule to DIR/lint-rules.json. Unless
--no-prove, it replays every rule against the repo's own history: a rule is
`proven` when it reports more hits at the mistake revision than at the fixed
revision (fix commit: sha^ vs sha; reverted commit: sha vs sha^).

Outputs: DIR/REFACTOR_PLAN.md, DIR/lint-rules.json, DIR/plan.json.
Needs the sibling `correct` skill (mine_mistakes.py, patlint.py).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime as dt
import json
import re
import shlex
import subprocess
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path


def correct_scripts() -> Path:
    here = Path(__file__)
    for base in (here.resolve().parent, here.parent):
        cand = base.parent.parent / "correct" / "scripts"
        if (cand / "mine_mistakes.py").is_file() and (cand / "patlint.py").is_file():
            return cand
    sys.exit("plan: needs the `correct` skill installed next to this one "
             "(skills/correct/scripts/{mine_mistakes,patlint}.py). Run install.sh from poteto-skills.")


CORRECT = correct_scripts()
sys.path.insert(0, str(CORRECT))
import mine_mistakes as mm  # noqa: E402
import patlint  # noqa: E402

TOKEN = r"`?([A-Za-z_][\w./-]*(?:\(\))?)`?"
CODE_TOKEN = re.compile(r"^(?:[A-Za-z_]\w*(?:\.[A-Za-z_]\w*)+(?:\(\))?|[A-Za-z_]\w*\(\)|[\w-]+\.(?:json|ya?ml|toml|csv|db|sqlite|txt|ini|cfg))$")
DATAFILE = re.compile(r"\.(json|ya?ml|toml|csv|db|sqlite|txt|ini|cfg)$", re.I)
SOURCE_EXT = re.compile(r"\.(py|js|jsx|ts|tsx|mjs|cjs|go|rs|rb|java|kt|swift|cs|php|c|cc|cpp|h)$")
GOOD_PATS = [
    re.compile(r"\b(?:use|call|via|through|prefer|switch to|route (?:it )?through|go(?:es)? through|must use|"
               r"should use|always use)\s+(?:the\s+|a\s+)?" + TOKEN, re.I),
    re.compile(TOKEN + r"\s+instead\b(?!\s+of)", re.I),
]
BAD_PATS = [
    re.compile(r"\b(?:don'?t|do not|never|avoid|stop|no more|shouldn'?t|should not)\s+(?:use\s+|call\s+|using\s+|"
               r"calling\s+)?(?:the\s+)?" + TOKEN, re.I),
    re.compile(TOKEN + r"\s+(?:file\s+)?(?:directly|by hand)\b", re.I),
]
INSTEAD_OF = re.compile(TOKEN + r"\s+instead of\s+(?:using\s+|calling\s+)?" + TOKEN, re.I)
USE_BEFORE = re.compile(r"\b(?:use|call|prefer|switch to)\s+(?:the\s+)?$", re.I)

ARCH_SIGNALS = re.compile(
    r"\b(directly|bypass\w*|instead of|go(?:es)? through|route[sd]? through|only (?:place|module|way|writer)|"
    r"single source|source of truth|owner\w*|duplicat\w*|copy[- ]?past\w*|two ways|old way|legacy|deprecated|"
    r"internal|private|hand[- ]?sync\w*|by hand)\b", re.I)
TYPE_SIGNALS = re.compile(
    r"\b(status|state|transition\w*|enum|none|null|nil|optional|invalid|illegal|typo|string literal|magic string|"
    r"stringly|types?|typed|schema|validat\w*|unrepresentable)\b", re.I)
TEST_SIGNALS = re.compile(
    r"\b(regression|crash\w*|broke|broken|returns?|edge case|off[- ]by[- ]one|500|exception|traceback|flaky|race|"
    r"wrong (?:result|output|value))\b", re.I)
TEST_GLOBS = ["**/tests/**", "**/test/**", "**/test_*.py", "**/*_test.py", "**/*_test.go", "**/*.test.*", "**/*.spec.*"]


def norm(tok: str) -> str:
    return tok.strip().rstrip(".,;:").removesuffix("()").lower()


def clean(tok: str) -> str:
    return tok.strip().rstrip(".,;:")


def vote_tokens(items: list[dict]) -> tuple[list[str], list[str], dict]:
    """Return (bad, good, detail) code tokens for a theme, by majority vote."""
    good, bad = Counter(), Counter()
    surface: dict[str, Counter] = {}

    def add(counter: Counter, tok: str, w: int) -> None:
        tok = clean(tok)
        if not CODE_TOKEN.match(tok):
            return
        key = norm(tok)
        counter[key] += w
        surface.setdefault(key, Counter())[tok] += 1

    texts = [it.get("text") or "" for it in items]
    for text in texts:
        for pat in GOOD_PATS:
            for m in pat.finditer(text):
                add(good, m.group(1), 1)
        for pat in BAD_PATS:
            for m in pat.finditer(text):
                add(bad, m.group(1), 1)
        for m in INSTEAD_OF.finditer(text):
            x, y = m.group(1), m.group(2)
            if USE_BEFORE.search(text[: m.start()]):
                add(good, x, 1)
                add(bad, y, 1)
            else:
                add(bad, x, 1)
                add(good, y, 1)
    mentioned = " ".join(texts).lower()
    diff_seen = Counter(norm(t) for it in items for t in set(it.get("diff_ids") or []))
    for it in items:
        if it.get("source") != "commit":
            continue
        added = {clean(t) for t in it.get("diff_added") or []}
        removed = {clean(t) for t in it.get("diff_removed") or []}
        only_added, only_removed = added - removed, removed - added
        kind = it.get("kind")
        bad_side, good_side = (only_added, only_removed) if kind == "reverted" else (only_removed, only_added)
        for t in bad_side:
            if norm(t) in mentioned or diff_seen[norm(t)] >= 2:
                add(bad, t, 2)
        for t in good_side:
            if norm(t) in mentioned or diff_seen[norm(t)] >= 2:
                add(good, t, 2)
    keys = set(good) | set(bad)
    margin = {k: bad[k] - good[k] for k in keys}
    bad_toks = sorted((k for k in keys if margin[k] > 0), key=lambda k: (-margin[k], k))
    good_toks = sorted((k for k in keys if margin[k] < 0), key=lambda k: (margin[k], k))

    def best(k: str) -> str:
        return surface[k].most_common(1)[0][0]

    detail = {best(k): {"bad": bad[k], "good": good[k]} for k in sorted(keys)}
    return [best(k) for k in bad_toks], [best(k) for k in good_toks], detail


def choose_level(items: list[dict], bad: list[str], good: list[str]) -> tuple[str, str, str]:
    """(level, why, why_not_higher)."""
    text = " ".join(it.get("text") or "" for it in items)
    arch = len(ARCH_SIGNALS.findall(text))
    typ = len(TYPE_SIGNALS.findall(text))
    test = len(TEST_SIGNALS.findall(text))
    if good and arch >= 2:
        return ("architecture",
                f"the evidence describes bypassing an owner ({arch} owner/bypass signals) and names the supported way `{good[0]}`",
                "already the highest level; keep the lint as a ratchet while call sites migrate")
    if typ >= 2:
        return ("types",
                f"the evidence is about values or states that should not be writable ({typ} state/type signals)",
                "no single owner or bypass is named, so moving code alone would not stop the bad state being constructed")
    if bad and good:
        return ("lint",
                f"a concrete bad pattern (`{bad[0]}`) and its fix (`{good[0]}`) are named, but no ownership or state change is implied",
                "no owner/bypass or state signal in the evidence; a lint whose message names the fix is the cheapest check that fails")
    if test or bad:
        return ("test",
                "the evidence describes behavior that broke, with no code pattern a regex can catch",
                "no owner, type, or lintable pattern is named; a behavior test through the public entry point is the highest check that fits")
    return ("docs",
            "no code token, owner, or state signal: this reads as a judgment call",
            "nothing in the evidence can be checked mechanically yet; write one AGENTS.md line with a failure example and re-run /correct when it repeats")


def slug(s: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", s.lower().removesuffix("()")).strip("-")[:40] or "rule"


def owner_module(good: str) -> str | None:
    core = good.removesuffix("()")
    if DATAFILE.search(core):
        return None
    if "." in core:
        return core.split(".")[0]
    return None


def derive_rule(n: int, title: str, items: list[dict], bad: list[str], good: list[str]):
    bad = [b for b in bad if b.removesuffix("()") not in {g.removesuffix("()") for g in good}][:3]
    if not bad:
        return None, "no bad code pattern named in the evidence"
    if not good:
        return None, "the evidence never names the fix; choose the owner API (/architect) before adding a lint"
    paths = [p for it in items for p in (it.get("paths") or [])]
    exts = Counter(m.group(1) for p in paths for m in [SOURCE_EXT.search(p)] if m)
    include = [f"**/*.{e}" for e, _ in exts.most_common(2)] or ["**/*"]
    exclude = list(TEST_GLOBS)
    owner = owner_module(good[0])
    owner_globs = [f"**/{owner}.{e}" for e, _ in exts.most_common(2)] if owner else []
    exclude = owner_globs + exclude
    parts = ["\\b" + re.escape(b.removesuffix("()")) + "\\b" for b in bad]
    regex = parts[0] if len(parts) == 1 else "(?:" + "|".join(parts) + ")"
    rid = f"no-{slug(bad[0])}" + (f"-outside-{slug(owner)}" if owner else "")
    bad_txt = ", ".join(f"`{b}`" for b in bad)
    owner_txt = f" ({owner_globs[0].removeprefix('**/')} owns this)" if owner_globs else ""
    message = f"Use `{good[0]}` instead of {bad_txt}{owner_txt}. Theme T{n}: {title}."
    rule = {"id": rid, "regex": regex, "include": include, "exclude": exclude, "message": message}
    return rule, None


def mistake_revs(it: dict) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
    sha, kind = (it.get("ref") or "")[:12], it.get("kind")
    if it.get("source") != "commit" or not sha:
        return None
    if kind == "reverted":
        return sha, sha + "^"
    return sha + "^", sha  # fix and revert commits: the mistake is in the parent


def count_hits(patlint_py: Path, rules_file: Path, repo: Path, rule_id: str, rev: str | None, paths: list[str]):
    cmd = [str(patlint_py), "--rules", str(rules_file), "--root", str(repo)]
    if rev:
        cmd += ["--rev", rev]
    cmd += paths
    res = subprocess.run([sys.executable, *cmd, "--json"], capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=str(repo))
    shown = shlex.join(["python3", *cmd])
    if res.returncode not in (0, 1):
        return None, shown, res.stderr.strip().splitlines()[-1:] or ["error"]
    data = json.loads(res.stdout)
    hits = [v for v in data["violations"] + data["expired"] + data["invalid_exceptions"] if v["rule"] == rule_id]
    return len(hits), shown, [f"{v['path']}:{v['line']}" for v in hits[:5]]


def prove(rule: dict, items: list[dict], rules_file: Path, repo: Path) -> dict:
    patlint_py = CORRECT / "patlint.py"
    inc = [patlint.glob_to_regex(g) for g in rule["include"]]
    proof = {"replays": [], "proven": False, "head_hits": None, "head_cmd": None}
    for it in items:
        revs = mistake_revs(it)
        if not revs:
            continue
        paths = [p for p in it.get("paths") or [] if any(g.match(p) for g in inc)]
        if not paths:
            continue
        bad_rev, good_rev = revs
        before, cmd, where = count_hits(patlint_py, rules_file, repo, rule["id"], bad_rev, paths)
        after, _, _ = count_hits(patlint_py, rules_file, repo, rule["id"], good_rev, paths)
        ok = before is not None and before > (after or 0)
        proof["replays"].append({"commit": it["ref"][:10], "kind": it.get("kind"), "mistake_rev": bad_rev,
                                 "fixed_rev": good_rev, "hits_at_mistake": before, "hits_at_fixed": after,
                                 "where": where, "cmd": cmd, "distinguishes": ok})
        proof["proven"] = proof["proven"] or ok
    n, cmd, where = count_hits(patlint_py, rules_file, repo, rule["id"], None, [str(repo)])
    proof["head_hits"], proof["head_cmd"], proof["head_where"] = n, cmd, where
    return proof


TARGETS = {
    "architecture": "Make `{owner}` the single owner: callers use `{good}`, nothing else touches what {bad} touched. "
                    "Hide or delete the second path (move the internals behind `{owner}`, delete copies an agent could imitate), "
                    "so a change that looks right from one file is right for the repo. Keep `{rule}` as a ratchet until no call site is left.",
    "types": "Model the values in this theme ({sig}) as a type the bad state cannot be written in: an enum or newtype plus "
             "one transition function owned by one module, validated once at the boundary. Callers stop passing raw strings.",
    "lint": "Add patlint rule `{rule}` whose message names `{good}`. Adopt a ratchet baseline if the pattern is already common.",
    "test": "Write one behavior test through the public entry point that reproduces the past failure ({refs}). "
            "It must fail on the mistake revision and pass on the fix.",
    "docs": "Judgment call: add one line to AGENTS.md with a concrete failure example from {refs}. Re-run /correct when it repeats.",
}
STEPS = {
    "architecture": ["Run /architect on the owner boundary: sketch the owner API ({good}) and the module layout, two candidates.",
                     "Route every call site through the owner; list them with the lint: `{lint_cmd}`.",
                     "Delete the old path and any helper an agent could copy.",
                     "Keep the lint with a baseline while migrating; drop the AGENTS.md rule once the lint makes the mistake unmergeable."],
    "types": ["Sketch the type (enum/newtype + transition table) with /architect.",
              "Convert the boundary (CLI/HTTP/storage parsing) to construct the type once; internal code takes the type.",
              "Make illegal transitions raise in one function; delete scattered string comparisons.",
              "Add a test that the illegal transition from the evidence is rejected."],
    "lint": ["Review the generated rule (regex, include/exclude) against the evidence.",
             "Run it on HEAD: `{lint_cmd}`; adopt a baseline if hits exist: add `--baseline .patlint-baseline.json --update-baseline`.",
             "Wire the same command into CI and the AGENTS.md rule table (`rule_table.py add`)."],
    "test": ["Write the failing test first against the mistake revision.",
             "Fix, then keep the test in the default test command."],
    "docs": ["Add the rule with an example to AGENTS.md (`rule_table.py add AGENTS.md --rule ... --enforced-by docs`).",
             "Expect `rule_table.py check` to flag it until something enforces it."],
}


def evidence_line(it: dict) -> str:
    return mm.describe_item(it)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="plan.py",
        description="Cluster feedback.json into themes and write REFACTOR_PLAN.md (evidence, pyramid level, target "
                    "design, steps, proof) plus lint-rules.json (patlint format) for lintable themes.",
        epilog="examples:\n"
               "  plan.py feedback.json --out-dir refactor/\n"
               "  plan.py feedback.json --out-dir refactor/ --no-prove --min-count 3\n"
               "then prove a rule by hand on a past mistake:\n"
               "  python3 <skills>/correct/scripts/patlint.py --rules refactor/lint-rules.json --rev SHA^ path/to/file.py",
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
    )
    ap.add_argument("feedback", type=Path, help="feedback.json from collect_feedback.py")
    ap.add_argument("--out-dir", required=True, type=Path, help="where to write REFACTOR_PLAN.md, lint-rules.json, plan.json")
    ap.add_argument("--min-count", type=int, default=2, help="minimum occurrences for a theme (default 2)")
    ap.add_argument("--threshold", type=float, default=0.3, help="cosine similarity to join a theme (default 0.3)")
    ap.add_argument("--repo", type=Path, help="repo for proofs (default: the repo recorded in feedback.json)")
    ap.add_argument("--no-prove", action="store_true", help="skip replaying rules against git history")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    if not args.feedback.is_file():
        print(f"plan: {args.feedback} not found; make it with collect_feedback.py", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    doc = json.loads(args.feedback.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    items = mm.review_items_from_json(json.dumps(doc), args.feedback.name)
    repo = (args.repo or Path(doc.get("repo") or ".")).resolve()
    can_prove = not args.no_prove and mm.is_git_repo(repo)
    out = args.out_dir
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    rules_file = out / "lint-rules.json"

    classes, unclassified = mm.cluster_items(items, args.threshold, args.min_count)
    themes, rules = [], []
    for n, c in enumerate(classes, 1):
        members = c["evidence"]
        title = " / ".join(c["signature"][:3]) or f"theme {n}"
        bad, good, votes = vote_tokens(members)
        level, why, why_not = choose_level(members, bad, good)
        rule, no_rule = derive_rule(n, title, members, bad, good)
        if rule:
            used = {r["id"] for r in rules}
            if rule["id"] in used:
                rule["id"] = f"{rule['id']}-t{n}"
            rules.append(rule)
        refs = ", ".join(m["ref"][:10] if m["source"] == "commit" else m["ref"] for m in members[:3])
        themes.append({"id": f"T{n}", "title": title, "count": c["count"], "sources": c["sources"],
                       "signature": c["signature"], "level": level, "why": why, "why_not_higher": why_not,
                       "bad": bad, "good": good, "votes": votes, "rule": rule, "no_rule_reason": no_rule,
                       "refs": refs, "evidence": members, "proof": None})

    rules_doc = {"rules": rules, "generated_by": "feedback-to-architecture/scripts/plan.py",
                 "source": str(args.feedback)}
    rules_file.write_text(json.dumps(rules_doc, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    if rules:
        try:
            patlint.load_rules(rules_file)
        except patlint.RulesError as e:
            print(f"plan: generated rules failed patlint validation:\n{e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        if can_prove:
            for t in themes:
                if t["rule"]:
                    t["proof"] = prove(t["rule"], t["evidence"], rules_file, repo)

    patlint_cmd = f"python3 {CORRECT / 'patlint.py'} --rules {rules_file} --root {repo} {repo}"
    lines = [
        "# Refactor plan: make repeated feedback impossible",
        "",
        f"Generated {dt.date.today().isoformat()} by `plan.py` from `{args.feedback}` "
        f"({len(items)} items: " + ", ".join(f"{v} {k}" for k, v in sorted(Counter(i['source'] for i in items).items())) + ")."
        f" Repo: `{repo}`.",
        "",
        "Each theme is a cluster of feedback seen at least "
        f"{args.min_count} times. Its level is the highest that can work: architecture > types > lint whose message "
        "names the fix > test > docs. Target designs are drafts; refine them with /architect before implementing.",
        "",
        "## Summary",
        "",
        "| Theme | Items | Level | Lint rule | Proof on history |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for t in themes:
        proof = "-"
        if t["proof"]:
            reps = t["proof"]["replays"]
            proof = (("proven on " + ", ".join(r["mistake_rev"] for r in reps if r["distinguishes"]))
                     if t["proof"]["proven"] else ("not proven" if reps else "no commit to replay"))
        rule_cell = f"`{t['rule']['id']}`" if t["rule"] else "none"
        lines.append(f"| {t['id']} {t['title']} | {t['count']} | {t['level']} | {rule_cell} | {proof} |")
    if not themes:
        lines.append(f"| - | - | - | - | no theme reached {args.min_count} occurrences |")
    for t in themes:
        r = t["rule"]
        fill = {"owner": (owner_module(t["good"][0]) if t["good"] else None) or (t["good"][0] if t["good"] else "the owner module"),
                "good": t["good"][0] if t["good"] else "the supported API",
                "bad": ", ".join(f"`{b}`" for b in t["bad"][:3]) or "the bypass",
                "rule": r["id"] if r else "a lint", "sig": ", ".join(t["signature"][:5]), "refs": t["refs"],
                "lint_cmd": patlint_cmd}
        lines += ["", f"## {t['id']}: {t['title']}", "",
                  f"Occurrences: {t['count']} ({', '.join(f'{k}×{v}' for k, v in sorted(t['sources'].items()))}). "
                  f"Signature: {', '.join(t['signature'][:6])}.", "", "### Evidence", ""]
        lines += [f"- {evidence_line(m)}" for m in t["evidence"]]
        lines += ["", "### Level", "",
                  f"**{t['level']}**: {t['why']}.", f"Why not higher: {t['why_not_higher']}."]
        if t["bad"] or t["good"]:
            lines.append(f"Named in evidence: bad {', '.join(f'`{b}`' for b in t['bad'][:3]) or '-'}; "
                         f"fix {', '.join(f'`{g}`' for g in t['good'][:3]) or '-'}.")
        lines += ["", "### Target design (draft)", "", TARGETS[t["level"]].format(**fill), "", "### Steps", ""]
        lines += [f"{i}. {s.format(**fill)}" for i, s in enumerate(STEPS[t["level"]], 1)]
        lines += ["", "### Proof", ""]
        if r:
            lines.append(f"Rule `{r['id']}` in `{rules_file}`: regex `{r['regex']}`, include {r['include']}, "
                         f"message: {r['message']}")
            p = t["proof"]
            if p:
                for rp in p["replays"]:
                    mark = "fires on the mistake and not on the fix" if rp["distinguishes"] else "does NOT distinguish mistake from fix"
                    lines.append(f"- {rp['kind']} {rp['commit']}: {rp['hits_at_mistake']} hit(s) at `{rp['mistake_rev']}`, "
                                 f"{rp['hits_at_fixed']} at `{rp['fixed_rev']}`: {mark}. Rerun: `{rp['cmd']}`")
                if not p["replays"]:
                    lines.append("- No commit in this theme touches a file the rule includes; prove it on a scratch "
                                 "copy of the mistake from the review comment.")
                lines.append(f"- HEAD: {p['head_hits']} hit(s) now"
                             + (f" ({', '.join(p['head_where'])})" if p.get("head_where") else "")
                             + f". Rerun: `{p['head_cmd']}`. After the refactor this must be 0, "
                               "or held by a ratchet baseline.")
            else:
                lines.append(f"- Not replayed (--no-prove or no git repo). Replay with patlint `--rev SHA^` on a fix commit's files.")
        else:
            lines.append(f"No lint rule: {t['no_rule_reason']}.")
            if t["level"] in ("types", "test"):
                lines.append("Prove the change with a test that fails on the mistake revision and passes after it.")
        lines.append("Record the enforcement: `rule_table.py add AGENTS.md --rule \"...\" --enforced-by \"...\"` "
                     "(from the correct skill).")
    if unclassified:
        lines += ["", "## Seen once (not a theme yet)", ""]
        lines += [f"- {evidence_line(m)}" for m in unclassified[:30]]
        if len(unclassified) > 30:
            lines.append(f"- … {len(unclassified) - 30} more in plan.json")
    (out / "REFACTOR_PLAN.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    plan_doc = {"version": 1, "feedback": str(args.feedback), "repo": str(repo), "themes": themes,
                "unclassified": unclassified, "rules_file": str(rules_file), "proved": can_prove}
    (out / "plan.json").write_text(json.dumps(plan_doc, indent=2, default=str) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    summary = {"out_dir": str(out), "themes": len(themes), "rules": [r["id"] for r in rules],
               "proven": [t["rule"]["id"] for t in themes if t["rule"] and t["proof"] and t["proof"]["proven"]],
               "levels": {t["id"]: t["level"] for t in themes},
               "files": [str(out / "REFACTOR_PLAN.md"), str(rules_file), str(out / "plan.json")]}
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Normalize review feedback into one list where every item names its source.

Inputs:
  --repo REPO           git history: fix commits, reverts, and the commits they revert
  --pr-comments JSON    PR review comments in `gh api` shape (body/path/line/user/html_url);
                        concatenated pages from `gh api --paginate` work too. Repeatable.
  --chat MD             chat or meeting notes in markdown; each bullet or paragraph is one item. Repeatable.

Output (--out, default stdout): {"version", "repo", "generated_at", "inputs", "counts", "items": [...]}
Each item: {id, source (commit|review|chat|code-comment), ref (sha, URL, or file:line), text, paths, line,
author, date, url, kind (commits: fix|revert|reverted), diff_added/diff_removed (commits)}.

Uses the item readers from the sibling `correct` skill (correct/scripts/mine_mistakes.py),
so /correct and /feedback-to-architecture read evidence the same way.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime as dt
import json
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path


def load_mine_mistakes():
    here = Path(__file__)
    for base in (here.resolve().parent, here.parent):
        cand = base.parent.parent / "correct" / "scripts"
        if (cand / "mine_mistakes.py").is_file():
            sys.path.insert(0, str(cand))
            import mine_mistakes  # noqa: PLC0415
            return mine_mistakes
    sys.exit("collect_feedback: needs the `correct` skill installed next to this one "
             "(skills/correct/scripts/mine_mistakes.py). Run install.sh from poteto-skills.")


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="collect_feedback.py",
        description="Normalize PR review comments, commit-history signals, and chat notes into one feedback.json "
                    "where every item has a source and a ref.",
        epilog="examples:\n"
               "  gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/pulls/comments --paginate > review-comments.json   # read-only\n"
               "  collect_feedback.py --repo . --pr-comments review-comments.json --chat chat-feedback.md --out feedback.json\n"
               "  collect_feedback.py --repo . --since 2026-07-01 --out feedback.json\n"
               "next: plan.py feedback.json --out-dir refactor/",
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
    )
    ap.add_argument("--repo", required=True, type=Path, help="repository (git history is read from here)")
    ap.add_argument("--pr-comments", action="append", type=Path, default=[], metavar="JSON",
                    help="PR review comments, gh api JSON shape (repeatable)")
    ap.add_argument("--chat", action="append", type=Path, default=[], metavar="MD",
                    help="chat/meeting notes in markdown (repeatable)")
    ap.add_argument("--since", help="only commits after this date (YYYY-MM-DD or git --since syntax)")
    ap.add_argument("--max-commits", type=int, default=2000, help="newest N commits to read (default 2000)")
    ap.add_argument("--no-git", action="store_true", help="skip commit history")
    ap.add_argument("--code-comments", action="store_true", help="also include HACK/WORKAROUND/FIXME/XXX comments")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, help="write feedback.json here (default: stdout)")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    mm = load_mine_mistakes()
    repo = args.repo.resolve()
    if not repo.is_dir():
        print(f"collect_feedback: {repo} is not a directory", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    items: list[dict] = []
    git_used = False
    if not args.no_git:
        if mm.is_git_repo(repo):
            items += mm.git_items(repo, args.since, args.max_commits)
            git_used = True
            if args.code_comments:
                items += mm.code_comment_items(repo)
        else:
            print(f"collect_feedback: {repo} is not a git repo; skipping commit history", file=sys.stderr)
    for f in args.pr_comments:
        if not f.is_file():
            print(f"collect_feedback: --pr-comments {f} not found", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        got = mm.load_feedback(f, source="review")
        for it in got:
            if it["source"] == "chat":  # a markdown file passed as review comments
                it["source"] = "review"
        items += got
    for f in args.chat:
        if not f.is_file():
            print(f"collect_feedback: --chat {f} not found", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        items += mm.markdown_items(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), f.name, "chat")

    seen, out_items, dropped = set(), [], 0
    for it in items:
        if not it.get("source") or not it.get("ref"):
            dropped += 1
            continue
        if it["id"] in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(it["id"])
        out_items.append(it)
    if dropped:
        print(f"collect_feedback: dropped {dropped} item(s) without a source ref", file=sys.stderr)

    doc = {
        "version": 1,
        "tool": "collect_feedback",
        "repo": str(repo),
        "generated_at": dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=0).isoformat(),
        "inputs": {"git": git_used, "since": args.since, "pr_comments": [str(p) for p in args.pr_comments],
                   "chat": [str(p) for p in args.chat]},
        "counts": dict(Counter(it["source"] for it in out_items)),
        "items": out_items,
    }
    text = json.dumps(doc, indent=2, default=str) + "\n"
    if args.out:
        args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        args.out.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        counts = ", ".join(f"{v} {k}" for k, v in sorted(doc["counts"].items())) or "no items"
        print(f"collect_feedback: wrote {args.out} ({counts})", file=sys.stderr)
    else:
        sys.stdout.write(text)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
